h: Step 1: Start the Main Story Quest (Green Quests)
Step 2: Do the Main Story Quest Until Level 50
Step 3 - Claim Your Catch Up Gear
Step 4 (Optional) - Continue the Main Story Quest (Getting to Auroria)
x: If you are interested in starting out on ArcheAge Classic, this is a somewhat in depth guide on how to set up the game, what your first few hours of gameplay will look like, and what you can expect going forward after reaching max level. Make sure to check out the Custom Server Changes page to see what makes ArcheAge Classic unqiue. If you're coming from legacy, check out the Joining Classic from Retail page as well. Installing For a quick video guide on installing ArcheAge Classic, watch: Installation & Donation Guide Please note: in regards to the installation video, the need to link your discord account to your in-game account is now no redundant and no longer required, you can ignore this step. To download the client go to aa-classic.to and make an account. Once you have made an account, click your profile name in the top right and navigate to the Download tab. Installation FAQ First Steps If you're still deciding what class you want to play, take a look at the Skill Trees page. Don't worry though, you can always change your skill trees and the Catch-up Gear Box gives you access to each type of gear set for different classes. Settings You'll want to get your settings in place before you start playing. It's recommended that all players take a few moments to set up their hotkeys/action bars, preferred functions etc. Once you do this, you will want to go to character select and then exit the game completely to ensure all of your settings are saved. If you forget this and crash, ArcheAge is notorious for resetting any changes you made but did not save by going to character select. Here are some QOL setting changes: Game Settings Name Info Disable Friendly and Enemy Pet/Summon Names Uncheck Display Nation Name Game Info Check Show Health Stats Check Show Mana Stats Check Close Tutorial (maybe not for brand new players!) Check View Frame Rate Set Quest Details Map Display to Unlimited Functionality Skill Deployment Location (This is a preference for many players, see what it does and decide if its for you) Disable Camera Shake Effects Disable Quest Dialogue Close-ups (Unless you're roleplaying/reading Lore) Learn where the "Disable Travel Through Other Players' Portals" option is, you'll want to use it when fighting against players trying to grief you. If your PC is slow, Show Default Player Appearances can be helpful for your gameplay experience. Disable Chat Filter, the game's innate filter makes a lot of words censored for no reason and its more harm than good. After that, set your Hotkeys how you like them, adjust your chat windows if you want. Then, go to character select and then exit the game (you will be glad you did). Step 1: Start the Main Story Quest (Green Quests) Yellow & Green quests; Quest Rewards This server has modified the Main Story Questline (green quests as many players will call them) compared to other servers to give players a few boosts as needed to propel them more quickly towards the more interesting part of the game. To level efficiently, you should only do green quests - find the first one for your race and follow the quest line. You will receive adventurer's growthstones as you progress through the story line to keep you leveled without having to do the zone quests (yellow). Continue doing green quests until you've completed the "Heading to Halcyona" Quest! For Haranya, there is a Portal in Caernord (Ynystere) that will Teleport you to Halcyona Nuia races can just walk south to Halcyona as needed Once you've Arrived in Solisa, you should be around level 37. Use all the Adventurer's Growthstones and open the last Equipment Gear Box of your choice before moving on! Each race usually throws a small "gotcha" during the main story quest, if you get stuck, feel free to ask in our community help section on discord, your friends, or read the quest flavor text as it usually has context on where you need to head next. If you've lost your green quest, try changing the Set Quest Details Map Display setting under Game Info to Unlimited. Also, when talking to Recruiter NPC's for quests, the Crimson Omen's Quest will have to be accepted first before the Green Quests you need shows up. Note: For the Warborn green quest "chapter 3 page 12", head back inside of the Inn and talk to the NPC with the yellow questmarker, complete it and it will progress onto the green quest once again. Step 2: Do the Main Story Quest Until Level 50 Where you'll be at the end of the core Main Story Quests After making it to Halcyona, the story quest is the same for all races. Most quests will be a "find this NPC" type quest. You'll want to continue these quests (Green Quests only) through Halcyona, Hellswamp and then Sandeep until you've completed the Quest: Across the Sea WARNING: These Zones (especially Halcyona) may sometimes be randomly littered with PvP and the Halcyona War Event, so your safety is no longer promised in these zones going forward. Once you complete this quest you'll be left staring out over the ocean (see image to the right). Use the rest of the Growthstones provided by the quest completion now until you are at least Level 45. Now you can use your Teleport Book to teleport straight Kroloal Cradle (Teleport Book -> Dungeons) for the next Green Quest. Zone into Kroloal Cradle and interact with the fire place just inside the entrance and continue following the Green Quest Line along. Once you complete the quest Arra's Ingriedients (flower requirement has been removed), use the new Growthstones given to you again now before moving on to the next step. This should get you level 50. To continue, take the portal at the top of the Veroe Tower to Karkasse Ridgelands. How to access marketplace mail Step 3 - Claim Your Catch Up Gear Congrats on reaching level 50 - you should automatically receive your Catch-up Gear Box in your inventory. Open it up and equip the gear for your desired class. It may be worth your time to read the Catch-up Gear portion of the Gearing Guide. There is information about gemming the gear provided and filling out your slots not filled by the catch up gear. Step 4 (Optional) - Continue the Main Story Quest (Getting to Auroria) Note: For Chapter 11.1, you can use a Bound Hereafter Stone, purchased from a general merchant, to complete this quest. You do not need to clear the Ocleera Rift. As a new player, you could go about your business however you want at this point. At Level 51, you will have no restrictions from playing normally - but it's recommended to continue the questline for some extra boosts in leveling until you've Reached the Following Quest: The Riven Gates. It is recommended that you stop your story quests once you get to the quests to craft an Obsidian Weapon. At this point, you will have also unlocked Chapter 99, which includes custom story quests to introduce players to certain world bosses and Activity Tokens. Once you complete 99.1, you should receive 1 Activity Token that can be used to unlock the Active Adventurers Appreciated daily merit quest. After that, you're all set to continue your adventures on AA Classic! It will take about 3-4 hours to get to the Riven Gates Quest with a moderate pace. Quicker if you have someone teleport to locations instead of having to make the walk. If you ever have any questions regarding anything else feel free to stop by the discord and ask the Player Helpers. Moving Forward The catch up bundle enables you to get started with almost any activity you want without the initial grind. Before you dive in too deep though, it's generally a good idea to get level 55. If you're a new or returning player, make sure to check out the list of common abbreviations you might see in chat, so that you don't miss out on any content. Leveling to 55 Levels 50-55 take significantly longer than 1-50. Level 55 unlocks key abilities and skill points for many skill trees. Some good ways to get XP at higher levels includes: Using labor (higher proficiency in the skill you use will result in more xp!) Sign Quests (daily, kill x mobs) in Golden Ruins Ayanad Library Dailies / Bosses Grinding mobs in Auroria Completing World Event quests PvP in War / Conflict zones Killing World Bosses (growthstones as a reward) Making Gold For more information, check out the Earning Gold wiki page. The primary method of making gold in ArcheAge is using your labor to farm, craft, do trade runs, and much more. There are many different viable ways to make money. Some may be more labor efficient, but take significant time investment, while others may burn through your labor faster, but net you less profit. You can explore different options in the folio (default keybind: "o"). An important concept to understand in ArcheAge is "Silver Per Labor (s/l)". For example, crafting 3 logs that each cost 5 silver into a piece of lumber you can sell for 25 silver, which costs 5 labor to perform would net you 10 silver for 5 labor - or 2s/l. Ideally you want to find a high silver per labor task that allows you to burn your labor in a manner that fits to your playstyle and the amount of time you play. Below is a list of some common money making methods. Take some time to figure out what fits your playstyle. Running trade packs Fishing Farming mob drops / coin purses Crafting Farming Auroria Land The more labor you invest into a given proficiency, the more labor efficient you will be doing those tasks are in the future. New Player Housing On ArcheAge classic special housing zones have been reserved for new and returning players, these areas apply special restrictions to who can build in them, helping players begin their journey into the world. You can find out where they are for your faction, as well as reading about these restrictions, on the New Player Housing page. World Events ArcheAge has many different events going on all throughout the day. World events are essential to progressing by earning honor and items such as Warrior Medals. They are also an important part of ArcheAge's gameplay, so make sure to try them out. Each faction will generally start a raid for each event and you will see peoplg x'ing up in faction chat for each given event. To see when each event is, check out the Event Calendar. PvP World Events The main focus of these events is PvP. Be ready to buff up and die. Golden Plains Battle (Halcyona) Mistmerrow Luscas Abyssal Attack Crystalline Bloodbath PvE World events PvP may not be the main focus of these events, but it can still happen at some. If it does, enjoy it! Crimson Rift (12:00 in game time) Grimghast Rift (00:00 in game time) Kadum / Hereafter Gates Ocleera Rift Gear The various gear options can be found in the Equipment Encyclopedia (default keybind "shift-i"). For more specific information about gearing, check out the Gearing Guide. You can find player-made starter gear sets on darugear.com. One way to get an idea of what your gear should look like is to take a look at someone who plays your chosen class on the top gear score list. You won't be able to copy them exactly, but it should give you a good idea as to what pieces you'll want in different slots. The gear you receive from the catch-up bundle should suffice while you get started on the server. Since it's pretty good gear, upgrades to it may be a bit expensive. Before spending a bunch of money on gear, make sure you have a reliable way to make more money. Crafted Gear This gear is crafted and tiered up in various ways, but generally with mana wisps and resources. Each time you tier up a piece of this type of gear, it has a chance to have one of many rolls which determines the stats the gear gives. Each piece has a specific roll that allows you to upgrade it to the next tier. Crafted gear of the same roll has set effects for 4-piece and 7-piece sets. This type of gear is tradeable at all times. Dungeon Gear Dungeon gear is initially acquired through dungeons and is a good source for early-game gearing as they have much higher chances of success when regrading. Generally, players will acquire armor pieces from Greater Howling Abyss (GHA), regrade them to Divine, then craft the piece into an Aria's Autograph which can be opened into a chosen piece of armor from Mistsong Summit (MSS) while maintaining the same grade. You will find that dungeon gear makes up the armor pieces for many of the starter gear sets on darugear.com. Dungeon gear is also notable for certain pieces that synergize well with specific classes. Most notably, almost every class is going to want serp sleeves for their arm slot. These are crafted by getting a full set of your class' from the dungeon Serpentis in Exeloch and combining them into a single piece that goes in your arm slot. You may also see melee classes using a Seastorm Tricorne from "Sea of Drowned Love" (otherwise known as Dahuta). Obsidian Gear Auroria Gear Example This gear is also crafted, but it is tiered up using mana wisps and mob drops rather than RNG crafting. There are no obsidian waist or arm pieces. At higher tiers, each type of obsidian armor splits into 2 trees you can pick from when tiering it up to provide different stats or passives depending on what your class wants. Obsidian gear binds on equip, but can be unbound by tiering it up. There are no obsidian accessories. World Gear World gear is gear acquired from mobs, world bosses, and various other sources. The gear in the catch up bundle is generally better than world gear. However, the catch up bundle does not provide players armor for their belt or sleeves slot. A cheap option to fill these slots early on is Lost Garden Gear. Open the Auction House -> Select Armor -> Search "Auroria" to view all these pieces. Lost Garden Gear provides decent stats and a equip passive that boosts a specific ability (see image). Generally, you will use a mix of various types of gear in your eventual gear set. Lunagems / Lunafrosts Lunagems and Lunafrosts can be bought from the honor shop. Lunagems (gems) slot into each armor piece and weapon you have and are extremely important for both gear score and actual gear effectiveness. Most importantly, you will want toughness and resilience gems in your armor as these will significantly improve your chance of surviving PvP encounters. Lunafrosts (frosts) provide an additional enhancement to each piece of gear with a specific enhancement based on the frost type. Weapons For most classes, it's generally a good idea to improve your weapon before your armor. Weapons have hidden passives that have a chance to proc when attacking. One handers Weapon Type Attack Speed Effect Dagger 1.4 Increases your attack speed for a short duration Sword 1.6 Parries the next attack received Katana 1.5 Your next attack will be a critical Axe 1.7 Regen health equal to 2% damage dealt for 3 seconds Club 1.8 10% chance to regen mana Scepter 1.8 Chance on hit to decrease cast time for 7 seconds Shortspear 2 Chance to greatly reduce the enemy's physical defense Two Handers Weapon Type Attack Speed Effect Greataxe 2.2 Chance to inflict bleed on the target for 14 seconds Bow 0.7 Chance to poison the enemy and to increase DPS by 15 for 15 seconds. Greatclub 2.2 Chance to stun enemy for 1.5 seconds Longspear 2.5 Chance to greatly ignore enemy defenses Nodachi 2 Chance for your next attack to be a critical attack Staff 2.3 Chance to restore a small amount of mana when inflicting magic damage Greatsword 21 Chance to parry the next attack when receiving damage Armor There are 3 types of armor: cloth, leather, and plate. Mages and healers usually go cloth. Melee and archer usually go leather. Some tank classes can run plate, but it's less common. Accessories Certain dungeon / quest line accessories are best in slot for certain classes such as: Halcyona Necklace Dream Ring Ynystere Ring Library Earring While working towards these pieces or to fill your remaining slots, use crafted accessories or accessories dropped as loot from mobs. Activity Tokens can also be exchanged for a decent set of accessories for starting players. Housing It's recommended you start working on housing after you are levelled up, as it can be a crucial component of your economy. For new players, New Player Housing is available to give you an easier time finding your first bit of land.

For class specific gearing guides, see Gearing: Class Specific Guides ArcheAge is comprised of 10 skill trees. After picking your first tree at level 1, second tree at 5, and your final tree at 10, you are given a class. These trees are changeable at any time, allowing dynamic gameplay, and changing your class is fluid. They vary in usefulness and purpose such as AOE (area of effect), DPS, burst, crowd control, mobility, etc.. Primary Trees Battlerage Skills based off of Physical Damage of main hand weapon. Close range. Single target. Nuke and crowd control. Passives provide melee critical bonuses, parry rate, damage, and damage reduction. This tree is intended to limit the abilities of one target with abilities like Lasso and provide damage reduction for their allies through the use of Sunder Earth, while being mobile enough to close the gap on enemies via Charge, Tiger Strike, and Behind Enemy Lines. Battlerage revolves around the use of Trip as a crowd control mechanic, and finishing off the target with Percision Strike Vitalism Skills based off of Healing Power. Damaging abilities count as Magic Damage. Long range single target healing. Healing over time. Close range AOE healing. This tree provides incredible healing with abilities like the single target heal Fervent Hearts, the AOE heal Mend, and heal over time Resurgence. Archery Skills based off of Physical Damage of bow weapon. Long range. Single target. Poke and Damage over Time. Passives increase ability range and movement speed. This tree excels at combat revolving around the ocean as its passives Wild Instincts and Marksman keep enemies at bay. Its staple ability, Endless Arrows, provides constant pressure on enemies. Sorcery Skills based off of Magical Damage. Long and close range. Single target and AOE. Nuke and crowd control. Passives decrease ability cast time, increase mana, and ability damage. Sorcery is incredibly useful at all stages of the game, providing single target damage like Arc Lightning, and AOE damage with Searing Rain. Its abilities Frozen Earth and Cold Feet keep enemies still as you blast them with Meteor. Secondary Trees Occultism Skills based off of Magical Damage. Close range. AOE. Crowd control. Channeled. Passives increase critical rate and ability utility. Combined with Sorcery, Occultism can keep a large number of enemies around you still for a long period of time. Hellspears stun enemies, effectively shutting them down for a few seconds. Summon Wraith and Summon Crows debuff their movement and attack speed, as well as ability accuracy. Shadowplay Skills based off of Physical Damage. Close and long range. Single target. Critical chance. Movement speed increase. Stealth. Fast ability attacks. Shadowplay can benefit any player as its Stealth ability allows them to escape certain danger in both PVE and PVP. It provides critical PVP abilities such as Stalker's Mark, reducing enemy healing, while also slowing up to 5 players while using Throw Dagger. It comes with a built in Trip via Overwhelm and Shadowsmite, as well as a poison to benefit Archery abilities. Witchcraft Skills based off of Magical Damage. Close range. Single target and AOE. Sleeps, fear, and a minion. Witchcraft is critical to players looking to excel in 1 on 1 combat with the use of Insidious Whisper and Lassitude. Banshee Wail can provide a quick escape, fearing an enemy should they get the upper hand. Fiends Knell is a minion that will help keep the enemy in check, allowing you to maintain the upper hand. Songcraft Skills based off of Healing Power. Close range. AOE. Benefits other players via use of Bard-like abilities. Contains critical bonus passives. Songcraft is an incredible tree, and essential for any raiding group. These players provide their entire raid with constant buffs with Songs, such as Bulwark Ballad for defense, Bloody Chanty for damage, Quickstep for movement speed, and healing via Ode to Recovery. Be warned, only the highest healing power should Ode as other players will reduce its efficacy. One of its final passives is Zeal, providing a massive critical damage bonus to anyone risking a glass cannon build. Defense Skills based off of Physical Damage. Close range. Single target and AOE. Invulnerability, damage reduction, self healing. Passives increase shield block rate against ranged and melee users, while abilities revolve around Mettle. Defense is what most would consider the tank tree. While tanking monsters in Archeage is not similar to other MMORPGs, it is the same concept of staying alive despite overwhelming odds. This is done with Invincibility to resist all damage for a time but stand still, Fortress to pull allies nearby and reduce their damage taken, and Redoubt to increase shield block rate as well as remove the ability to be stunned for XX seconds. Defense can also impede enemy mobility using Imprison, a magical wall summoned that cannot be walked through. Auramancy Skills based off of Magical Damage. Close range. AOE. Self buffs. Mobility. Passives provide invulnerability as well as reduced damage taken. An essential tree to all builds and should always be considered your third tree. It has abilities benefiting everyone. They benefit offensive potential with attack speed from Thwart, mobility with Comet's Boon, Teleport and Mirror Warp, and enemy control via Vicious Implosion, an AOE pull. It provides massive defensive benefits like magic resistance from Magic Shield and Wings of Protection, debuff protection from Shrug It Off and Liberation, and received damage reduction with Inspiration Cloak and Absorb Damage, and finally Unassailable, providing a chance at 3 seconds of pure invulnerability.

Obsidian gear is easy to craft gear with no RNG required to tier them up. Obsidian gear has unique bonuses on each piece. For armor, these bonuses often makes Obsidian armor the preferred choice. Tier 1 through 3 weapons can be crafted at the Anvil, while Tier 4 through 6 must be crafted at a Regal Anvil. Obsidian gear is intend to cater to specific playstyles and encourage build diversity, such as the Obsidian Shortspear and Obsidian Katan which provide healing power and magic attack respectively, in addition to the melee dps. Starting at Tier 4, Obsidian gear generally branches out in two separate paths. For example, obsidian cloth gear allows the player to choose whether or not they want healer gear with more spirit, or mage gear with more intelligence.

AAClassic is a unique server as it runs on a much older version (3.5) than retail, on top of having its own set of custom changes. Below is a list of notable custom changes on AAClassic that make it more fun and fair than other servers. Marketplace The Marketplace on AAClassic does not contain "Pay to Win" items unlike other servers. Only a few quality of life additions border the line of P2W (i.e., inventory slot increases, Daru Subscription Box), otherwise everything else is cosmetic. Vocation & Economy Replanting Replanting is a unique AAClassic feature. On some harvestables, you will find an interaction that allows you to harvest the resource and use a seed/sapling to put a new one in its place automatically. This quality of life feature is meant to make farming bundles and other resources much less manual labor and means players can spend more time in the world instead of having to spend precious time manually planting their fields. Higher Labor & Rates AAClassic runs on a higher labor rate of 40 labor every 5 minute (offline AND online). AAClassic also has boosted labor consumption rates AND yield rates on activities such as sports fishing and commerce. This allows you to burn your labor and make money faster, reducing the amount of grind required. Schematic Scraps Ship component designs can now be evenstoned for Schematic Scraps. Schematic Scraps can be used to craft specific ship component designs that may otherwise be hard to find. New Recipes Special recipes have been added to a variety of items such as Regrade Charms, Lucky Points, Lunarite and more. Because these items were primarily sourced from P2W RNG boxes previously, such recipes were added to make them farmable & part of the economy. Custom Buffs Custom recipes for buffs have been added to help free up buff slots and also provide an easier way to obtain loot drop buffs. You can find the recipes in the Folio menu 'o' by default. Monarch of the Sea (1hr): Kingdom's Shadow + Dahuta's Bubble effects. Select between +1800 Physical, Magical, or +810 Physical/Magical defenses. Spellbook: Bulwark / Spellbook: Authority (1hr): Unstoppable Will + Secret Gift + Honor Goblet. Select between an defensive or offensive spellbook and include the stats you need the most! Pigglewiggle Feast / Pigglewiggle Stew (1hr, 10 uses): Assorted Ribs + Jujube Juice + Jujube Sparkling Wine. Select between a delicious feast to boost your strength and agility or delight in a savory stew to increase your intellect and spirit. Glittering Charcoal Milk (1hr): Grants you 20% increased loot drop. Mysterious Glittering Charcoal Milk (1hr): Grants you 50% increased loot drop. Events Mistmerrow Mistmerrow has an added kill quest to encourage PvP at the event that provides additional rewards. Mistmerrow has been shortened from a duration of 30 minutes down to 20 minutes. Crystalline Bloodbath The Crystalline Bloodbath is a completely custom event that currently takes place every Friday that calls all who are interested to PvP in Diamond Shores, a common occurrence back in the old days of ArcheAge. Completing the event will provide you with 30 Activity Tokens as a reward. Preparing for the Fish Market Every Saturday you can get a Fishing quest from any Fish Stand to fish and sell 10 fish to get 20 Activity Tokens. The Crimson Threat Every Sunday you can get a quest in Sungold, which requires to kill Anthalon once. Completing this quest provides 15 Activity Tokens Veroe Harvest Harvest Festival event where factions fight over rice drops from flowers to deliver packs in certain location in Hasla. Faction that takes the most packs on drop location first wins. Meteor Landing At random timers, roughly once per day, a comet lands somewhere in the world, triggering waves of monsters and bosses. Map areas Swirling Meadows Swirling Meadows as an area and extra land for housing in Ahnimar and Rokhala Mountains. Snowfang Isle Snowy village in Miroir Tundra called Snowfang Village area with its own housing style. Gearing Crafted Seals Similar to 3.5, AAClassic has items called "Mana Seals" which can be crafted with the reforging proficiency. They require varying mana wisp costs and allow a player to take any Epherium+ gear piece and make it a Sealed item again. This allows attempting to get the desired outcome, whether it be an upgradeable piece or a specific stat roll, but is not guaranteed. Honor Economy On AAClassic, most honor items have been made tradeable. This allows players to acquire honor gems without needing to get honor yourself. This also allows making gold by farming and selling honor. The 2nd gem slot is also a 100% slot rate. Prestige Economy On AAClassic, most prestige gems have been made tradeable. This allows players to acquire prestige gems without needing to get prestige yourself. This also allows making gold by farming and selling prestige. Obsidian Materials Tradability In an effort to promote a free market, AAClassic has set all obsidian materials as unbound. This allows players to farm obsidian materials as an extra revenue source. Ships Pufferfish Ship The Pufferfish Ship (sometimes called 'Puffership') is a small artillery warship equipped with a giant cannon pointing forwards. It has an elevated move speed when heading North or South. It's driving style is quite different from other boats and will require shorter impulses when turning, at the risk of flipping over. Luxury Liner This absolute beast of a ship is available for players to make and use! It is very costly, slow but truly magnificent. Misc Additions Location of the Casino Mirage Casino The Mirage Isle casino is located immediately behind the building where you will spawn in Mirage Isle. Previously, the Mirage Isle casino was disabled in retail versions of the game due to EU gambling laws. Now enabled, you can purchase Bugira Coins from the merchant in the centre of the casino. Using these coins, you're free to interact with either of the 3 types of slot machines available for a chance to win up to 150x your bet. The three types of slot machines have three separate prices, the base tier costing 1x Bugira coin per spin, the second costing 5x Bugira coins per spin, and the final costing 10x Bugira coins per spin. An achievement set has been enabled with this, with the final reward being the title "Gambling Addict". Merit Quests Know as AAA the Active Adventurers Appreciated are custom added Merit Quests. Only these Merit Quests give small amount of Activity Tokens once completed with XP and gold. To activate them player needs to spend few Activity Tokens. Addon System AAClassic is the first server to have brought out an addon system. You can read more on the addons page Addons Custom Weapon Skins Competitions held by the Darus for the community to create custom weapon skin designs to make as weapon in the game world.

h: How to Claim Your Catch-up Gear Box
x: The Catch-up Gear Box enables you to get started with almost any activity you want without the initial grind. It provides decent starter gear, as well as various items to get you started making money and progressing your character. Marketplace Mail How to Claim Your Catch-up Gear Box Reach level 50 and your catch-up gear box will automatically appear in your inventory. For healers, you will likely want to convert the mage cloth pieces to healer cloth pieces at a Soulforged Anvil. The recipe "Conversion: Soulforged..." can be found in the folio. The Vitalism skillset is symbolized by Kyprosa, who was tasked with guarding the gate to the dream realm rather than participate in reality. Now, her disciples heal and revive fallen allies rather than participate in bloodbaths themselves, providing crucial life support in battle. Optimized for combat support, Vitalism was designed for experienced users who can nimbly switch between different weapons for attacking and healing. Masters of this skillset can shift the tide of battle by healing their allies, or turn their power on themselves to survive nearly any assault. Every Friday, an event starts that allows you to take a quest from your respective faction's capital city at the Shadow Daru NPC. Kill 50 enemies in Diamond Shores to complete the quest and receive 30 activity tokens. For Pirates the kills required is reduced.

Larceny in ArcheAge refers to the profession centered around farming monsters for profit. This is a great, simple profession for new players as there is no upfront investment required. The loot from monsters is a mix of coin purses, crates, and random gear that can be salvaged for archeum. Auroria Lodestone on the map Players can grind noble, jester, prince, and queen's purses and crates with scaling difficulty of the monsters. Noble crates and purses are found in mid tier zones main continent zones (Sanddeep, ...) Jesters crates and purses are found in higher tier main continent zones (Karkasse, ...) Princes crates and purses are found in all Auroria zones. Queens crates and purses are found around purified lodestones in Auroria. Zones that are in conflict or war have higher loot drop rates. In ArcheAge, fishing can refer to two types of activities: Bait fishing and sport fishing. Bait Fishing Bait Fishing is the act of using a fishing rod, bait worms and casting your line in any body of water. It will reward various types of fish, which can be sold as they are, chopped as chum for fishing spots or turned into Dawn Lake essence Sport Fishing Sport fishing has two different forms, freshwater (inland lakes, ponds) and saltwater (out at sea). As of patch 1.2.5 any chopped fish bucket (excluding squid) can be used on a saltwater fish pool to activate it. Chopped squid is used for fresh water sports fishing. When you get a fish on the line a sequence minigame starts where you need to match the skill to the debuff of the fish at the time. An example would be if the debuff for "Stand Firm Left" shows up you press that button. The process is the same for the other skills as well. The main skills you should not miss are "Big Reel In" and "Reel In", these are the primary skills for dealing damage to (catching) the fish. Ice Fishing Ice fishing can be done in the Mirror Tundra. Advanced Fishing Advanced fishing is the final feature of fishing where you use "Ground Fish Chum" to bait fish within the Sunspeck Sea for "Big Belly Fish". These fish act similiar to crates where they have a loot table when you open them and can give you items like treasure maps, and Solzreed Mackeral that convert 3 fish to 1 Dawn Lake Essence among various other items. In order to Advanced Fish you need a rod capable of doing it as well as max proficiency in fishing. Classic-only Changes Compared to the standard 3.0 version, Classic has had the following changes: "Old" fishing pools. They expire on duration instead of fish count and have a predetermined fish type. If you find a Marlin pool, it can be a lot of gold! Doubled Labor usage & Gold reward: With the increased labor quantity on Classic, the labor and gold ratio of fish was adjusted to make it feel more rewarding and less of a grind New Fishing Rods: The rods introduced later in the game were backported to let players choose between Cast Time or Damage. Or, if they are rich enough, the Ultimate rod which mixes both! Timers on Pools: Pools will show the timer before they expire at all time, instead of requiring players to write it down Labor Split: Instead of the labor being all on the fish catch, part of the labor is moved to turn-in to make getting pirated a lesser loss for fishers Universal Chum: Compared to 1.2 pools, here all fish types eat all types of chum! Sunfish Schools: On rare occasions, once a feeding frenzy ends a Schooling Sunfish can appear. Chumming it will alert the entire world, so be prepared for a fight!

ArcheAge is home to six major races: the spiritual Nuians, secretive Elves, and crafty Dwarwes share the western content, while nomadic Firran, cunning Harani, and fearsome Warborn inhabit the continent to the east. Loose ties connect the neighboring races, but allegiances are fluid, forever complicated by the whims of pirate factions sailing, trading, and pillaging at will. In ArcheAge Classic some racial skills have been replaced with other race's skills in order to balance them out. Nuian Alliance Nuian "We fear no death." Called the Conquerors of the Continent, Nuians possess a deeply spiritual culture that revolves around worshipping Nui, the Goddess of the Hereafter. They revere the traditions, beauty, and harmony of their fallen kingdom, and fight fearlessly to bring these traits to their new land. Racial skills Explosive Expert Instant 30min cooldown Increases ship/tank Cannon damage +3% for 5min. Nui's Blessing Instant 30min cooldown Nui's Blessing increases Strength, Spirit, Intelligence, Stamina, and Agility +8% for 5min. Effect gradually decreases. Can't be used during Nui's Consolation buff. Elf "The blood of life is Honor, and the blood of death the same." Elves seclude themselves deep in the forest, avoiding other races as much as possible. Though envied for their beauty, their behavior is considered incomprehensible: hoping for an honorable death, they often deliberately seek out danger. They feel the ultimate honor is vengeance for their past defeats. Racial skills Lithe Flow Instant 30min cooldown Increases swim speed +5% and allows you to hold your breath underwater for 30 more seconds for 5min. Earth Lover Instant 30min cooldown Increases the Maximum Health of nearby allies mounts +10% for 5min. Dwarf "Raze foes. Raise cities. Rejoice in stone." Known for being independent and inventive, Dwarves largely withdrew from the rest of the world following the Demon War. But with the recent rise of their old foes, the Warborn, the Dwarves are returning to Erenor places and politics, bringing new technology with them. Most people assume the Dwarves simply want to keep the Warborn in check, but Dwarven motivation-- and ambition--are rarely so simplistic. Racial skills Catlike Reflexes Instant 30min cooldown Negates falling damage for 5min. Dwarven Artifice Instant 30min cooldown Decreases Machining production time -30% for 5min. Haranyan Alliance Harani "We may bend, but we do not break." Harani are survivor in the truest sense of the word. Others may do anything to succeed, and meet their gods in the process, but Harani will do anything to live. Practical, cunning, and family-minded, it is no surprise the strength of their new kingdom rivals the strength of the kingdom they lost. Racial skills Jungle Tamers Instant 30sec cooldown Decreases the time required for logging trees and gathering herbs -30% and resets Recall cooldown for 5min. Explosive Expert Instant 30sec cooldown Increases ship/tank Cannon damage +3% for 5min. Firran "Claw to earth, blood to water, fang to wind, fur to fire." The restless, nomadic Firran roam the wilds, fueled by dreams of protecting nature and reclaiming their former glory. They believe every life --no matter how small-- is not only valuable, but plays a critical role in the natural world, and that every Firran must strive to find their purpose and play their part. Racial skills Strong Claws Instant 30min cooldown Enables you to climb trees and ladders 50% more quickly and increases Move Speed +10% during a Dash for 5min. Catlike Reflexes Instant 30min cooldown Negates falling damage for 5min. Warborn "Always, we will rise. Always, it is dawn." Once slaves to their demonic nature, the Warborn slaughtered thousands. Now, they seek to atone for these sins. However, their need for redemption has left them as little more than servants to new masters. Perhaps one day, penance complete, they will find a way to be truly free. Racial skills Lithe Flow Instant 30min cooldown Increases swim speed +5% and allows you to hold your breath underwater 30 more seconds for 5min. Brute strength Instant 30min cooldown Increases Move Speed +10% while carrying trade packs for 5min.

In ArcheAge Classic there are plenty of different mounts to collect. Most of them can be obtained by playing the game: obtained from point shops, from npcs or various events and custom questlines. Some mounts can be bought from Marketplace, but those are nerfed versions, meaning they have less skills than other mounts or same or less speed that other mounts have to eliminate the possibility on using real money to gain advantage. Since there are so many mounts it is easier to categorize them by how to obtain them so the pages are easier to read and not clutter with endless list. Some mounts can be obtained various ways. Jousting Lances are used when performing Jousting Lance Charge skill on Black Arrow mount, which can break ally and enemy imprisons. Skill consumes one Jousting Lance every time it is used. Jousting Lances can be crafted on normal Anvil with 15 Iron Ingots and 5 Lumber.

The Daru Subscription Box is a monthly box that can be obtained for 1000 credits in the marketplace. This box is purely "Pay for Convenience" containing no items that provide any true advantage for players. Daru Subscription Box contents: (30 Day) Any-Post Owl, Summons Owl Mailbox (30 Day) Anywhere Warehouse, Summons a warehouse manager (30 Day Buff) Blessing from the Darus -50% Portal Cast Time -50% Embers Cast Time -50% Recall Cast Time +10,000 For all Language Proficiencies Shorter "Good Night's Sleep" duration Auction House listings show Seller's name Can summon Lanayu, Blessed Frog x1 Golden Token, These can be redeemed on the marketplace Award > Golden Token. Commerce is a profession centered around delivering trade packs to specific merchants. Both crafting and delivering these packs costs labor granting proficiency in Commerce. Reaching 230k commerce proficiency grants the title Barter $auce giving 20 Intelligence and 10 Spirit when equipped. When crafted these packs can be picked up and put into vehicle pack slots or simply carried on a players back, slowing their movement speed. Different trade routes have a variety of risks and reward values letting players customize the amount of risk they are willing to accept for gold. Based on your pack and route, the trader NPC you will turn in your pack to will pay you a percentage ranging from 130%-70% of each pack's set turn in value. You can check this percentage using the trade info menu (Shift-O) and selecting your route. You can view each pack's turn in value here: Trade Run Pack Values Pack Types There are 3 main types of packs, Specialty, Fertilizer, and Larders. Specialty and Fertilizer pack crafting recipes can be found in the folio by going to Commerce → Haranyan/Nuian Specialties. Specialty packs can be crafted at each zone's specialty workbench, which can be found on the map by filtering Infrastructure → Specialty Workbench. Some specialty packs require Gilda Dust to craft, making them a bit more expensive, but with a unique percentage from the turn in NPC. These packs have no additional restriction on where they can be turned in any trader that accepts any other pack type will also accept a Gilda Pack. Each zone also has a Fertilizer pack which is unique in two ways. All Fertilizer packs have the same crafting recipe, they require 25 chopped produce, 25 ground grain, 20 trimmed meat, and 50 dried flowers. Additionally, Fertilizer Packs can not be crafted at a zone's Specialty Workbench, instead they must be crafted at a special kind of player owned home called a Tradesman Manor, players must either build their own, find one set to public, or join a guild/family that has a private one. Larders require a different crafting process than other packs. These can not be found in the folio, what can be found is a Multi-Purpose Aging Larder players must first either buy these off other players or craft them themselves. Then the larder is placed on land, filled with aging materials and let to sit for 3 days. Once 3 days have passed they can be picked up and turned in like a regular pack. The type of aging material used determines the type of larder that is produced — larders aged with milk and lemon make cheese packs, honey and straw bundles make honey packs, cultivated ginseng and olives make salves. Due to the elevated price of cultivated ginseng players generally do not craft salve packs. Rewards Gold trader icon on the map Trade packs can be turned in at three different types of merchants: Gilda Traders, Gold Traders, and Resource Traders. Gold Traders reward gold, Gilda Traders reward Gilda, and Resource Traders reward Charcoal Stabilizers. The Freedich Resource Trader gives Dragon Essence Stabilizers instead of Charcoal Stabilizers. With the exception of Freedich, gold and Gilda traders only accept trade packs made on the continent they were crafted in. Freedich gold and Gilda traders accept packs made on any continent. Turn in values are calculated based on a couple factors: A pack's base value, this is predetermined by the game, and differs depending on where the pack was crafted, what kind of pack it was, and where the pack is being turned in. Generally the farther it is between two zones, the higher the base turn in value. Turn in percent, this modifier is applied to the base value and ranges from 70% to 130%. As players turn in packs, the percent for that pack type and origin location slowly decreases, making the packs less valuable. As time passes the percent will slowly creep back up until it is capped at 130%. The current percent at any trader can be viewed in game by hitting shift o. Its important to note that each pack type has its own percent, unique to where it was crafted, what type of pack it is, and where it is being turned in. Solis cheese larders turned in to Two Crowns wont affect the percent of Solis honey larders also being turned in to Two Crowns. The only way to increase the turn in percent is to wait. Turn in Locations While most Nuian and Haranyan zones have gold and Gilda traders there are 8 turn in locations that get used the most: Freedich, Solis, Villanelle, Ynystere, Falcorth, Two Crowns, Cinderstone, and Solzreed. Each zone has one turn in location with the exception of Ynystere and Cinderstone which have two turn in locations. A map of each of these turn ins can be found here Common Turn in Locations Freedich Gold Trader Twice daily the Freedich Gold Trader event starts spawning a Gold Trader on Freedich Island. As a general rule of thumb this trader gives the highest reward per pack of any trader in the game. However, turning in at this trader is quite risky due to being a limited time event, and the general nature of PvP on Freedich. Specific Runs Double Peace Trade Run Sunbite to Solis Trade Run Perinoor to Solis Trade Run West to East Trade Run Yny to Freedich Trade Run Rokhala to Solis Trade Run

In ArcheAge Classic there are many different currencies for different uses. It can get overwhelming fast, so, here is explained some of them and their usages. Permanent Tokens Currency Icon Obtained from Usage Credits Credits can be bought with real money through under Donate tab on the Website Profile. Marketplace Golden Token Replacement to old Daru Tokens. Golden Tokens can be obtained by buying Daru Subscription Box from the Marketplace. One box will give one Golden Token. Marketplace > Award > Golden Token Loyalty Token Once online the game provides 3 Loyalty Tokens every 60 minutes (up to 3 times a day). Marketplace > Award > Loyalty Token Gilda Star Daily quests and other activities. Marketplace > Award > Gilda Star or Mirage Island Merit Badge Merit Quests and certain Achievements. Marketplace > Award > Merit Badge Login Badge In the Login Tracker once you have completed the whole month the last reward is 1 Login Badge. Login Badge Reward NPC in the middle at Mirage Island once you enter. Activity Token Sources of Activity Tokens The desk is located on the left side once you enter Mirage Island. Can be used to buy scrolls, decent starting trinkets, Synthium stones, Gilda Stars, Warrior Medals and to craft mounts. Priceless Coin How to get Priceless Coins? The blue machine is located on the right side once you enter Mirage Island. With these coins you can buy a 30-day mounts or gliders that can be upgraded into permanent one with Activity Tokens. Player Appreciation Coin Loyalty / Homecoming Chest that was given as a gift for old and returning players. Warrior Medal Warrior Medals can be obtained from daily quests like Halcyona War, Mist Merrow etc. Warrior Medal crafting bench can be found in each factions bases. Use these medals to craft necklace and instruments and also to upgrade cloaks. Comet Shard Comet Shards are obtained from mining and finishing the quests related to Starfall event. Broom Race Coin Given to those participated in the Hallowtide event on Mirage Island. Broom Race event during Hallowtide Festival. Mirage Island. Blue Ribbon Coin Awarded to those who've performed well in the farming contest. Basically placing Experia items on your land and gathering them gives points for you in the Blue Ribbon leaderboard. The leaderboard resets every week and the end of the week rewards will be sent. As a reward you can get gold and Blue Ribbon coins, the amount based on your performance with growing Experia items. The Blue Ribbon NPC can be found -once entered to Mirage Island- on the right side. The NPC sells some furniture items. Fisher King Coin Awarded to those who've performed well in fishing competitions; can be exchanged for various items. The Blue Ribbon NPC can be found -once entered to Mirage Island- on the right side. The NPC sells some decorative items and fishing trinkets. They can be earned through: Family quests Blue Salt Merit quests Community Center Daily quests Remodeled House quests Farmer's Workstation Meal quests Press C > and the cart image next to Vocation Badge icon. The Fishing quest named 'Preparing for the fish market' can be obtained from any Fish Stand on Saturdays. Often, players will do this in raids concurrent with the Mirage Isle Fishing Contest event, which is also on Saturdays. However, you have whole week to complete the quest, and you need to catch and sell 10 fish to get the quest done. Tip: You can complete this quest faster if you do it in a party or in a raid, since all of the fish sold to vendor (not those crafted into decor items) count toward quest total for all party/raid members.

In game time Archeage Classic has a various amount of daily activities, this guide will go through most important ones and more of them will be added as the server progresses. Crimson Rift - CR Crimson Rift better known as CR is one of the most common daily activities, you can join the raids for this activity by X-ing up in the Faction/Nation chat when groups are being made. It will reward you with 1000 Honor Points and 10 Leadership. CR Nuia Spawn Locations This event takes place every 4 hours at 12:00 in game time. To check the time you can hover over the top right corner of your screen. CR Haranya Spawn Locations Take quests can be picked up from one of the guards in the Community Center and they will need to be returned once completed to acquire the rewards. This event is mostly PvE where you will defend against 3 waves of monsters and 2 bosses (Hounds) at the end. The Hounds have a quest of their own, killing one of them will reward you with 3 Guilda Stars 2 Clear Synthium Shards and 7 Adventurer's Growthstone. Bellow it will be shown the starting location of the rift and the end position where people will go to complete their quests and the most common callouts used to point the raid in the right direction. Grimgast Rift - GR Community Center GR 1st quest Grimgast Rift better known as GR is one of the most common daily activities, you can join the raids for this activity by X-ing up in the Faction/Nation chat when groups are being made. This event takes place every 4 hours at 00:00 in game time. To check the time you can hover over the top right corner of your screen. The first quest you take from the wooden board in the Community Center and it will require you to deliver 10 materials to a NPC, these materials can be: stone brick, lumber, leather, fabric, iron ingot. After handing in the materials it will give a 2nd quest that requires you to deliver 2 packs to the trebuchet. 1 - Pick up quest from Community Center | 2 - 1st quest completion and pack spawn location Bellow it will be shown the locations for and steps for GR quests completion. GR Haranya Quest Location Once the trebuchet is built you can pick up a harpoon that will help you kill the mobs for the quest. The quests auto complete after the mobs are defeated. GR harpoons rack Needs to be removed with "Time of Oblivion" harpoon skill After the two waves of mobs are defeated 2 hounds will spawn and each one will give you a quest reward. These ones have a special mechanic that will require the use of the 2nd skill on the harpoon to deal with it. Mistmerrow - MM Mistmerrow is a PvP event between Nuia, Haranya and the Pirate faction, where the three of them compete over the control of the towers in the map. The towers spawn in each basin of the map and need to be destroyed in order to be claimed. Mistmerrow Map At the start of the event you can get to Mistmerrow through one of the portals located in Capital Cities like Marianople (Nuia) and Austera (Haranya) Mistmerrow portal Before going inside, talk with the NPC in front of the portal and pick up the 2 quests. These will reward you with Honor Points, Warrior Medals, Clear Synthium Shards and Leadership. One of the quests will be completed once you talk with the NPC in Mistmerrow and you will receive an additional quest that will require you to kill the towers inside. After Mistmerrow battle is done the zone will go in peace and 2 additional quests will appear at the NPCs in the middle, these will require to kill 3 gates that spawn in SE/W/NE Basins and Kadum that spawns in the middle of the map. Halcyona War Halcyona War is a PvP event centered around destroying the enemy factions base. Halcyona Map Pickup the first quest from the Capital City of your faction and enter the portal or teleport to with your own portal to Halcyona. There in your faction camp you will turn the first quest in and pickup a second quest that will require you to kill 10 enemies (this quest can be completed in a party or a raid). The quests for this event reward you with Honor Points, Clear Synthium Shards, Warrior Medals and Leadership. Once a faction destroys the enemy's base crystal you can loot the crystal for a Warrior Medal Chest that will reward between 5-10 Warrior Medals. If victorious you can return to the Community Center and pick up a buff that will last 2h. Luscas Lusca spawn locations Lusca is a water PvP event located between Auroria and Freedich Island. You can pickup the quest from the NPC located in Diamond Shore Ezi's Light. The quest will reward you with a good amount of Honor Points, 1 Gilda Star, Shatigon's Sand and Leadership. Lusca fight

The Costume Spreadsheet is really useful tool to plan out your costumes and undergarment stats. Stat costumes How to get Stat costumes can be bought from guild shop and they cost 200 Prestige points. There are 4 different types of costumes depending what class you play. Upgrading For upgrading the stat costume you need Synthium Stones. First you need Synthium Shards which you drop easily by doing Daily activities. 10 Synthium Shards combine into 1 Synthium Stone. You always need 2 Synthium Stones to add the EXP to the item. Once the items EXP bar is full you can either choose to keep the stat and improve it or roll for another stat. You should always try to roll the bad stats away first. Later on you can use Serendipity stone to change the stat but those stones are expensive. Applying costume images Start by opening you inventory and clicking the third button with sword and arrows. This will open Item Fusion tab. When changing the Stat Costumes appearance to one of your costumes make sure the costume has been made into Image Item. If it's not, you can buy one Fusion Alembic from any General Merchant or Marketplace with Credits. Make sure the Sat Item is the one on the left slot, otherwise it will be destroyed. Once completed the Stat costume will have the costume image, aka you will have the stats with nice appearance. This can be always reverted if you want to. You need just 1 Extraction Alembic from any General Merchant. Go to the same tab as before but take the Extraction tab. The Stat Costume and appearance costume will both be returned and they can be used again. Undergarments How to get Undergarments you can get from Evenbards. Evenbards spawn to the factions main cities and other locations during the night. There are also 4 different kind of Undergarments depending what class you play. Once you obtain undergarments you need to buy also 20 Honor Badges from Honor Shop or do Arenas to get them. Upgrading Synthium Soap Stat costumes and Undergarments have timer of 30 days and after that the stats become unavailable and by washing them you get the stats back on track. Soap can be purchased from any General Merchant or Marketplace. Synthium Stones Synthium stones can be crafted from Clear > Vivid > Lucid > Radiant. The recipes can be found in game by pressing O (Folio). The higher the grade of the item the higher stones it needs. Synthium Stones can also be bought with Activity Tokens. Clear (basic) Synthium stones can be looted from world bosses and crafted by combining 10 Synthium Shards which are acquired when completing various boss kill quests.

World bosses are big mobs that players usually gather for in order to drop good loot like gear, mounts etc. Some of them are part of questlines and need to be killed / looted for ques items. Few of the Lesser Bosses an be tamed as pets. World Bosses can be put in 3 categories: Major World Bosses, World Bosses and Minor World Bosses Major World Bosses Major World Bosses in ArcheAge are bosses that usually fit one or more of the following: Exceptionally difficult High value loot Contested over in PvP on practically every occasion Have static spawn times to encourage grouping up and preparing for them Major World Bosses Name Level Location Description Kraken 50 West of Arcadian Sea A giant squid. As an ocean boss, it only receives damage from ships. Red Dragon 50 Karkasse Ridgelands With multiple flying and ground phases, it requires a lot of preparation. Improved version of Hanure the Hunter Thunderwing Titan 55 Reedwind Colossal Titan, which can be summoned in Reedwind. Anthalon 50 Sungold Fields Spawns after Sungold CR. x: Hamilton's Gearing Guide Video Use the gear Folio (default keybind Shift-I) to explore different gear and its stats. Feel free to gear however you'd like. Note that this guide is player made and may be subject to debate. The information provided should still help you get an idea how to gear relatively efficiently but it may not be optimal for you. Step 0) Pre-Level 55 Don't worry about your gear too much during this time. You will basically use whatever you get from the story quest and mob drops while questing. This gear will all be quickly replaced. Divine Armor Grade Bonus Step 1) Catch-up Gear Once you reach level 50, you will receive your catch up gear. Open the box for your desired class' gear and equip it. The catchup gear does not include a piece for your waist or arms slots, so you will want to find any cheap piece of world gear to use in these slots that has stats that fit your class. For now, make sure you keep these pieces at Rare or below or else they will disrupt your Armor grade bonus (see image for example and more info). A cheap, but good option to fill these slots early on is Lost Garden Gear. Open the Auction House -> Select Armor -> Search "Auroria" to view all these pieces. Lost Garden Gear provides decent stats and a equip passive that boosts a specific ability for each skill tree depending on the piece. The catch-up gear also does not include accessories. You may farm some cheap ones off mobs while leveling or you could just buy them from the auction house. Activity Tokens can also be exchanged for some decent starting accessories. The catchup box also comes with some starter gems, you will want to gem your catch up gear with Toughness (legs) and Resilience (chest). These stats will increase your odds of survival in PvP encounters significantly. The first 2 slots have a 100% chance of slotting, so use the tier 4 (pink) gems for these slots. For all the remaining slots, use tier 3 (blue gems) as they continue to have a 100% success rate on the remaining slots while tier 4 gems do not. You could technically use tier 4 for these slots, but you may break all your gems and waste a lot of time gemming gear you should be planning on replacing! Check out the Gemming Guide if you need additional guidance. For gemming your other pieces, it may be better to just save up until you upgrade out of your catch-up gear rather than sinking more money into gear you should aim to replace. Upgrading Catch-up Gear Once you get some Activity Tokens from participating in various events, talk to any Daru Auctioneer by a Mirage Isle portal to start the quest for upgrading your catch-up gear. It may be a good idea to wait until you upgrade your catch-up gear before you put gems in the chest/legs, but it's not a big deal if you have to re-gem them. You will need to locate the Soulforged anvil which can be found in Diamond Shores. Step 2) Divine Dungeon Gear & Hasla Weapon Weapon After you've completed your initial leveling, new players are advised to start working on their Emerald Weapon (Hasla Weapon) until it reaches Divine grade. Armor For your armor pieces, a cheap way to get decent armor pieces is to acquire Divine Dungeon Gear. This is due to the fact that dungeon gear is considered "Easy" to regrade when you look at the Regrade Rates for different types of gear. Players can acquire armor pieces from Greater Howling Abyss (GHA), regrade them to Divine, then craft the piece into an Aria's Autograph which can be opened into a chosen piece of armor from Mistsong Summit (MSS) while maintaining the same grade. You will find that dungeon gear makes up the armor pieces for many of the starter gear sets on darugear.com. Gemming your gear is an important step in order to survive in PvP encounters. Specifically, you will want to slot Radiant Earth Lunagem: Mastery lunagems in your pants to increase your Toughness stat, and Radiant Earth Lunagem: Flexibility lunagems in your pants to increase your Resilience stat. See the Gemming Guide for a quick overview on how to gem your gear. Accessories This is also a good point to get started on your Dream Ring quest line if it's a good fit for your class. Healers may prefer the Ynystere Ring. Most classes will also want to start working on their Halcyona Necklace. These pieces mentioned above mostly require time and effort rather than gold, so you are able to work on them while saving up gold to upgrade your other gear. To fill in your other accessory slots, consider library accessories, mob drop accessories, or some cheap crafted accessories. As for your other accessories, don't spend too much gold as upgrading your other gear further will be a better bang for your buck. Step 3) Crafted & Obsidian Gear, Serp Sleeves As you're gearing, if you aren't sure what to upgrade next, check out Gearing#Class Specific Guides or take a look at other players and the top 100 gear score list to see what gear and gems other players may be going for your class! Crafted & Obsidian Gear Once you've completed your "Early Game" (cheap) set of dungeon gear, it's time to start working on more expensive pieces to improve your gear. For this stage in your gearing process, you will generally want these pieces to be Divine or Epic grade, but don't think you need to regrade them yourself as it is often times cheaper to purchase the pieces from other players instead. Generally, a more finalized gear set will include a mix of gear types. For example, some classes may prefer all Obsidian gear pieces, but there are no Obsidian pieces for the waist or arm slots, so players will fill these slots with Crafted, Dungeon, or Auroria gear pieces. Obsidian gear is tiered up through simple crafting recipes fount in the Folio (default keybind: "o"). Crafted gear is tiered up through a more RNG based crafting system, see Reforge, Regrade, and Manaseal Guide. For Obsidian gear, you will want to tier it up based on what grade of gear you acquire. For example, Epic Obsidian gear is often upgraded to T6, while Divine Obsidian gear is often only upgraded to T5 or T4, as the price of tiering it up becomes much more significant at higher tiers. For gear pieces at this stage, since they are worth much more money, consider investing more into things like Gems or Tempers. Make sure you upgrade them to the maximum tier before doing this, as the crafting process will remove any modifiers to the gear (excluding the item grade). Serp Sleeves For MOST people and classes, you will use obsidian gear for most of your pieces (certain players may prefer crafted gear for specific classes). However, there are no obsidian pieces for the waist and arm slots, so you will have to use either world gear or crafted gear. For example, most classes will use "Serp Sleeves" in their arm slot. Mages and healers will generally use a Cruel-Glory Sash in their belt slot while other classes may prefer a crafted belt or an Auroria belt with a bonus to a specific ability. Ask around, browse the gear score list, see what best fits your class and playstyle. Generally Viable Gear Class Gear Type Setup Mage Cloth Obsidian gear for your main 5 pieces, Serp Sleeves + Cruel Glory Sash or a crafted sash. Melee Leather Obsidian gear / 4 piece Gale/Flame for your main 5 pieces, Serp Sleeves + crafted belt. Archer Leather Obsidian gear / 4 piece Gale for your main 5 pieces, Serp Sleeves + crafted belt. Healer Cloth Obsidian gear for your main 5 pieces, Serp Sleeves + Cruel Glory Sash or a crafted sash. Tank N/A N/A If you don't know what these words mean, read the Gearing section on the Getting Started page and rest of this guide. Once you've upgraded your weapons, chest, and legs, go ahead and continue upgrading your other pieces. Once upgraded, consider gemming them with either crafted or prestige gems. Prestige gems are called Lunascales and have a 100% slot chance, whereas crafted gems are only 100% on the first 2 slots. Some players will use crafted gems for their first 2 slots, as they offer larger bonuses but are more expensive, and then use prestige gems to fill the remaining slots. Prestige gems are also tradeable and can be bought from other players. If you haven't already, now is a good time to upgrade your accessories, instrument, bow, and other off pieces. Costume and Undergarments Since your gear is pretty good once you complete Step 3, it may be more cost efficient to start progressing your costume and undergarments before going for additional gear upgrades. Step 4) Repeat Step 2 & 3 But With Better Gear Next on the list may be an Epic Ayanad Weapon, Epic Tier 7 Weapon, Epic armor, or a Legendary weapon if you're super rich or lucky. If you get to this point you don't need to be using this guide most likely.

The Ynystere Ring is a questline ring often used by healers. Getting the quest starter You can obtain the Stone Orb from the end boss of any Greater Dungeon. It drops for everyone in the party and is a 100% drop chance. Right click to start the quest. The Strange Stone Report to Archeologist Burnar on Freedich Isle. (You will need to ride your boat here or ask someone for help. It is a contested PvP Area) A Fellow Collector After talking to Archeologist Burnar he will send you to Apprentice Rudal who is located in Exeloch. Rudal's Favor Rudal will now send you to Diamond Shores to talk to Drillmaster Raysen. Consulting an Expert Drillmaster Raysen will send you to Nuimari to talk to Archeologist Hermas who will give you "The Kidella Ring Manuscript". You will need to craft the Manuscript you received into a "The Kidella Ring" book and then place it in a house that you own then interact with the book to received the next quest. (You can use someone else's book if you do not have a house to put it in.) You will need 10 paper, 1 Memory Ink and 5 Leather to craft the book. The Stuff of Legends After Interacting with "The Kidella ring" book, You will need to head back to exeloch to talk to Apprentice Rudal again. The Ringbearer Apprentice Rudal will send you to Asaji who is at the top of Veroe in Hasla. Take the elevator to reach the top if you can not find her. Asaji will ask you to rescue Princess Surya who is in Kroloal Cradle. You will need to do the whole dungeon including the last boss to get her to spawn. DO NOT LEAVE AND FORGET TO TALK TO HER. Talk to Asaji and accept the next quest. A Dangerous Curse Simply Return to Apprentice Rudar in Exeloch and you will receive the Arcane Ynys Guardian Ring. Restoring the Ring Apprentice Rudar will now send you to Archaeologist Hermas in Nuimari again, You will then be sent to speak to Belstrom in Diamond Shores. A Purifying Spell Belstrom will ask you to collect a pretty hefty list of items to purify the ring. x: Introduction Auroria is the North most continent in the world of ArcheAge and is for adventurers typically level 50 and higher. Auroria Continent Auroria has 10 different zone to live in and explore. Each with their own perks and downsides. Diamond Shores Golden Ruins Sungold Fields Calmlands Marcala Heedmar Nuimari Exeloch Reedwind Mistmerrow Getting to Auroria Auroria Portal found in major cities Getting to Auroria is pretty easy. There is a portal in Multiple locations all over the Eastern and Western Continent. On the east continent a portal can be found in Austera in the Solis headlands and in Caernord in Ynystere. On the west continent a portal can be found in Marianople and in Seachild Wharf in Cinderstone Moor. You can also find a portal on the Pirate island of Growlgate in the Stormraw Sound. The portal will have 2 options. The first being to the housing area and the second being straight to the faction base. You can also just sail there from either continent if you are up for the boat ride but it is a LONG ride. Castles One of the major features of Auroria (and ArcheAge in general) are the castles that you will find on Auroria. They are owned by the guild that has claimed it in the most recent siege cycle which occurs every X weeks. Players can earn Lord Coins by working on the territory and completing various quests. Bidding on a Castle's Siege Scroll (wip) Burning Logs and Mineral Waters Certain zones have naturally spawning resource nodes, otherwise known as "logs" and "waters", which are unique ways to take advantage of owning land in Auroria. They are generally contested by other players and you will have to fight to claim them. Logs spawn in Calmlands and Marcala, and can be used to light Regrade Braziers for a chance to get Sunpoints, Moonpoints, and Starpoints. Waters spawn in Heedmar and Nuimari, and can be used to water Archeum Trees for a chance to get Moonlight, Sunlight, and Starlight archeum. Alternatively, players can use Lord Coins to craft a Blazing Tree or Mineral Water Pump that they can place on their land. After an initial timer, these will become a source of 10 of the respective resource. This is a much less risky and reliable way to take advantage of your Auroria land, but the cost of the Lord Coins comes out of your profit!

Regular scrolls can increase an items grade by 1, while resplendent scrolls have a chance to increase it by 1 or 2 grades. Regrading beyond Celestial grade can result in your item breaking or downgrading. Easy - Applies to equipment dropped from Dungeons. Normal - Applies to all other equipment. Difficult - Applies to crafted and obsidian equipment, as well as Items dropped by Worldbosses. Grade Easy Normal Difficult Ship/Pet Basic -> Grand 100% 100% 100% 100% Grand -> Rare 100% 100% 100% 60% Rare -> Arcane 100% 100% 100% 60% Arcane -> Heroic 67.5% 50% 32.5% 60% Heroic -> Unique 67.5% 50% 32.5% 60% Unique -> Celestial 47.3% 35% 22.8% 50% Celestial -> Divine 40.5% 30% 19.5% 50% Divine -> Epic 13.5% 10% 6.5% 40% Epic -> Legendary 10.8% 8% 5.2% 35% Legendary -> Mythic 4.1% 3% 2% 17.5% Resplendent Regrade Scrolls Resplendent Scrolls are made using a Lucky Point (Sun/Moon/Star) alongside' its corresponding Regrade Scroll Using a Resplendent Scroll will add an additional chance upon success of upgrading an item twice, resulting in, for example, a Celestial >> Epic regrade in one go. Having a Success on any regrade using a Resplendent Scroll gives a 20% bonus chance (1 in 5) of going up an extra grade. x: ArcheAge NA/EU Retail has been announced to shut down on the 27th of June 2024. Following this news, a lot of ArcheAge Retail player may be looking to join Classic as they would like to keep playing. Due to the numerous differences between Retail and Classic, this page compiles changes & differences to help you get settled into our own version of Erenor In the meantime if you're looking at just jumping in, check out the Getting Started page! This page is a work in progress and more information will be added Major Differences Below you will find a list of differences between Classic and Retail. These are not all the differences but should give you a quick overview Custom Patches 1.2, 1.3 and 1.3.5 You may hear a lot of talk about patch 1.2, which refers to Berserker's Awakening (Patch 1.2) 1.3 refers to Patch 1.3 which is a custom version of retail patch 3.5 1.3.5 refers to Patch 1.3.5 which is the first patch in the Starfall Saga Gearing Hiram and Erenor gear do not exist in Classic. Instead, we use Obsidian and Ayanad gear sets. The way to grow these gear sets is very different. Instead of doing dailies to grind your Hiram gear, you will instead focus on making gold to regrade, upgrade, or purchase gear. Gems are also set on the old "Make it or break it" system. All gems will break if you fail gemming past the second slot! Skill Trees Classic does not have all Skill Trees that retail did. You will not find the following trees here: Gunslinger Malediction (Note: Abyssal Skills are enabled and contain the Malediction skills, spread over all trees) Swiftblade Spelldancer Economy Regrade Charms and Lucky Points are crafted items Obsidian mats, library mats, and honor gems are all tradeable. Commerce The Commerce system on Classic is the "old" commerce which means: No Cargo Packs or Freshness value on trade packs Packs can be crafted anywhere and turned in anywhere Gold Trader on Freedich still exists You can acquire Gilda Stars and Charcoal Stabilizer (equivalent to Onyx Essence) via cross-continental trade runs, Dragon Essence via Freedich Runs and Gold via same-continent runs Labor & Gold rates have been adjusted as part of Custom Changes. Packs use more labor but give more gold. Fishing You can check the Fishing page for all information. Key difference: Each Fish School has a predetermined fish type. A Marlin school of fish will give Marlins. Custom Events This server has a variety of custom events and changes to existing events to make them more fun. Some include: Updated Mistmerrow includes a boosted kill quest to encourage more PvP and less running in circles. Veroe Harvest Festival, a custom faction PvP event which is a capture the flag like objectives. Crystalline Bloodbath, a PvP event every Friday where everyone comes to duke it out in PvP at Diamond Shores to earn activity tokens. Custom Changes You can find a more general overview of changes on the Custom Server Changes page. Here are a few notable ones: Seed Bundles, Coral and Trees can be replanted using a custom feature. This allows spending less time doing tedious work on farms, and more time enjoying the game No P2W, no Alting Classic has a strong commitment to not including P2W items in the cash shop. The admins also actively enforce rules against RMT and alting in order to keep the server as fair as possible. Because of these changes, patron is free and housing its not restricted to paying users. Frequently Asked Questions Is land available? While the answer here varies over time, currently there are open land spots all over the world. This will change with the influx of new players How is Faction Balance? Factions are relatively equal, with variance depending on Time of Day due to Classic's international nature as opposed to being a strictly EU/NA server. There is a rough split of 48.5% of players in each faction with a 3% population of players in Pirates Is the Patron subscription required? Patron is free for everyone! There is only an optional QoL subscription that does not grant advantages How long has the server been open? ArcheAge Classic opened on the 4th of August, 2023 There are no plans on closing the servers like KakaoGames'

Starter mounts or so called "race mounts" are the mounts that each race gets on the start of the game. All starter mounts can be bought with any character. Starter mounts need to be bought from the place each race starts their journey. All these mounts need to be raised to adults before they can be used. Evenbards are NPCs that spawn during night in major cities of Nuia and Haranya and they are selling items, that cannot be found anywhere else. They spawn between 22:00 and 8:00 in-game time on random locations in six large cities. Since their location is randomly chosen between several spots in each city, best way to find them is use /target name command in chat. Here is list of Evenbards and their cities: Locations of Evenbards Nuia Haranya Samiel (Crescent Throne) Samion (Marianople) Samunin (Sanddeep) Yariz (Mahadevi) Nirha (Lutesong Harbor) Aragi (Ynystere)
