Shows an in-game style tooltip for a glider, fetched from the sermeatball API. Usage {{Glider|8001101}} The only required parameter is the item ID of the glider. The data is read from data pages stored on the wiki (Module:Data/Gliders/..., made by sync_wiki_data.py). A glider that is not stored yet is read live from the API until the script has been run for it. The icon is the game's own icon of the glider (from the glider API); if that file is not on the wiki, the file named after the glider is used. The name, description and the flight stats (speed, gliding, turning, launch height, special skills) come from the API, with the colours of the game. float (optional): where the card sits on the page. right or left places it at that side with the text flowing around it, center centres it. Leave it out for a normal card in the flow of the page. Each special skill gets its own row, and is hoverable. The skill IDs come from the glider part of the API (/wiki/glider/<id>), matched by skill name. A skill the API does not list is shown as coloured text. Module:GliderSkillIds is optional now: an ID written there is only used for a skill the API did not give. use (optional): replaces the "Use:" text. Normally the standard glider text is used, and Magithopters (descriptions with "Air Speed") get the Magithopter text. The "Equip effect" text is written in the module. Needs Module:Glider, Module:IconName, Template:Grade, Template:GliderSkillRow, Template:GliderSkill (and through it Module:Mount and Template:Mount/styles.css) and Template:Glider/styles.css. Examples {{Glider|8001101}} {{Glider|8001101|float=right}} No description. Template parameters Parameter Description Type Status Item ID 1 The item ID of the glider, for example 8001101 Number required Position float Optional. Where the card sits on the page: right or left (text flows around it) or center. Leave empty for a normal card in the flow of the page. Suggested values right left center String optional Use text use Optional. Replaces the "Use:" text of the card. Leave empty to use the standard text. String optional

local p = {} local IconName = require('Module:IconName') local Store = require('Module:DataStore') -- data stored on the wiki by sync_wiki_data.py local Mount = require('Module:Mount') -- its hover box for a skill -- Optional manual list: skill name -> skill ID. Only used for skills the API did not give an ID for. local okIds, SkillIds = pcall(require, 'Module:GliderSkillIds') if not okIds or type(SkillIds) ~= 'table' then SkillIds = {} end -- "Glider Charge" and "glider charge!" are the same skill local function key(s) return (tostring(s or ''):lower():gsub('[^%a%d]', '')) end -- The skills as sent by Template:Glider: "id¦name‖id¦name‖..." -> key(name) -> id local function parseSkillIds(str) str = tostring(str or '') local ids = {} if str:find('class="error"', 1, true) then return ids end for _, row in ipairs(mw.text.split(str, '‖', true)) do local f = mw.text.split(row, '¦', true) local id, name = tonumber(mw.text.trim(f[1] or '')), mw.text.trim(f[2] or '') if id and name ~= '' and not ids[key(name)] then ids[key(name)] = math.floor(id) end end return ids end -- Make text safe to put inside HTML / wikitext local function esc(s) return mw.text.encode(tostring(s or ''), '<>&"\'%[%]{}|') end local function trim(s) return mw.text.trim(tostring(s or '')) end -- Colours of the game's short codes: |nc;...|r is orange, |ni;...|r is yellow ("Immune to |ni;Turbulence|r"). -- Other short codes (|nd; |nr; ...) are shown without colour. local NCODE = { c = 'FF9C27', i = 'F5CB65', d = 'A3E3FD' } -- The game marks highlighted words as |cFFRRGGBB...|r. -- Only those parts get a colour, the rest keeps the card's text colour. local function coloured(text) text = tostring(text or '') text = text:gsub('|n(%a);(.-)|r', function(code, inner) if NCODE[code] then return '|cFF' .. NCODE[code] .. inner .. '|r' end return inner end) local out, pos = {}, 1 while true do local s, e, rgb, inner = text:find('|c%x%x(%x%x%x%x%x%x)(.-)|r', pos) if not s then break end out[#out + 1] = esc(text:sub(pos, s - 1)) out[#out + 1] = '' .. esc(inner) .. '' pos = e + 1 end out[#out + 1] = esc(text:sub(pos)) return table.concat(out) end -- Where the card sits on the page (float parameter), set inline so it works without the style page local FLOATS = { right = 'float:right; clear:right; margin:0 0 0.5em 1em;', left = 'float:left; clear:left; margin:0 1em 0.5em 0;', center = 'margin:0 auto 0.5em auto;', } -- The "Use:" texts of the game (not part of the API). Magithopters have their own text. local USE_GLIDER = 'Equip a glider to glide from place to place. You can only use glider skills while airborne and will be knocked off your glider if attacked.' local USE_MAGITHOPTER = 'Equip wings to use Free Glide. You can only use glider skills while airborne, and will be knocked off your glider if you are struck by an effect that prevents movement. You will remain airborne if attacked. Gliding disables Parry, Evasion, and Shields; increases Received damage +50%.' -- key(name) -> id for the skills of a stored glider local function storedSkillIds(stored) local ids = {} for _, s in ipairs(stored.skills or {}) do if s.id and s.name and not ids[key(s.name)] then ids[key(s.name)] = math.floor(s.id) end end return ids end -- The stat lines of a glider description. Some descriptions (Arkana Wings) have no blank line between the -- story and the stats, or even write the stats after each other on one line, so a line that starts with one -- of these labels is where the stats begin. local LABELS = { 'Flight Speed', 'Air Speed', 'Gliding Ability', 'Cruising Ability', 'Turning Speed', 'Sheering Speed', 'Launch Height', 'Ascension', 'Special Skills?', 'Special Note' } local function startsWithLabel(line) for _, l in ipairs(LABELS) do if line:find('^' .. l .. ':') then return true end end return false end -- puts every label on its own line local function splitStats(desc) for _, l in ipairs(LABELS) do desc = desc:gsub('(%S)[ \t]+(' .. l .. ':)', '%1\n%2') end return desc end -- "Special Skill: Glider Charge, Instant Acceleration" -> one row per skill. -- A skill with an ID (from the API, or Module:GliderSkillIds) gets a hover box. local function skillRow(frame, label, value, apiIds) local row = mw.html.create('div'):addClass('aa-glider-skillrow') row:tag('span'):addClass('aa-glider-skilllabel'):wikitext(esc(label) .. ' ') local box = row:tag('div'):addClass('aa-glider-skills') local function add(rgb, name) name = trim(name) if name == '' then return end local html local id = apiIds[key(name)] or SkillIds[name] local sk = id and Store.get('Skills', id) if sk then -- the skill's data is stored on the wiki: no request needed html = Mount.hover({ args = { name = name, realname = sk.name or '', color = rgb or '', cd = sk.cd or '', cast = sk.cast or '', mana = sk.mana and tostring(sk.mana) or '', desc = sk.desc or '', icon = sk.icon or '' } }) elseif id then html = frame:expandTemplate{ title = 'GliderSkill', args = { id = tostring(id), name = name, color = rgb or '' } } elseif rgb then html = '' .. esc(name) .. '' else html = esc(name) end box:tag('div'):wikitext(html) end local found = false for rgb, inner in value:gmatch('|c%x%x(%x%x%x%x%x%x)(.-)|r') do found = true -- the data may colour several skills as one piece ("Rocket Launch, Divebomb") for _, name in ipairs(mw.text.split(inner, ',', true)) do add(rgb, name) end end if not found then -- no colour codes in the data: split at the commas for _, name in ipairs(mw.text.split(value, ',', true)) do add(nil, name) end end return tostring(row) end -- A failed API request (with "suppress error" in the template) leaves External Data's own error text -- behind. Treat that as "no data" instead of showing it. local function fetched(s) s = trim(s) if s:find('class="error"', 1, true) then return '' end return s end function p.card(frame) local a = frame.args local stored = Store.get('Gliders', a.id) -- live data: read the skill list first, the hover boxes fetch data of their own later local apiIds = stored and storedSkillIds(stored) or parseSkillIds(a.skills) local name = stored and trim(stored.name) or fetched(a.name) if name == '' then return '' end local grade = stored and trim(stored.grade) or fetched(a.grade) local hasGrade = not (grade == '' or grade == 'None' or grade == 'Any') if not hasGrade then grade = 'Basic' end -- no grade: Basic look, and no grade line local desc = (stored and trim(stored.desc) or fetched(a.desc)):gsub('\r', '') local float = trim(a.float):lower() if not FLOATS[float] then float = '' end local isMagi = desc:find('Air Speed', 1, true) ~= nil local category = stored and trim(stored.category) or fetched(a.category) if isMagi then category = 'Magithopter' elseif category == '' then category = 'Glider' end local use = trim(a.use) if use == '' then use = isMagi and USE_MAGITHOPTER or USE_GLIDER end local root = mw.html.create('div'):addClass('aa-glider') if float == 'right' or float == 'left' then root:addClass('aa-glider-float') end if float == 'right' then root:addClass('aa-glider-right') end if float ~= '' then root:attr('style', FLOATS[float]) end -- header: icon, category, grade, name local head = root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-glider-head') head:tag('div'):addClass('aa-glider-icon'):wikitext(IconName.icon({ args = { name, grade, size = 48, file = stored and trim(stored.icon) or fetched(a.icon) } })) local title = head:tag('div'):addClass('aa-glider-title') title:tag('div'):addClass('aa-glider-cat'):wikitext(esc(category)) if hasGrade then title:tag('div'):addClass('aa-glider-grade'):wikitext( frame:expandTemplate{ title = 'Grade', args = { grade, esc(grade) } }) end title:tag('div'):addClass('aa-glider-name'):wikitext( frame:expandTemplate{ title = 'Grade', args = { grade, esc(name) } }) root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-glider-sep') -- description: the first paragraph is running text (the data may break it into short lines), -- every line after the blank line (Flight Speed, Special Skill ...) stays on its own line local lines = mw.text.split(splitStats(desc), '\n', true) local intro, i = {}, 1 while i <= #lines and trim(lines[i]) ~= '' and not startsWithLabel(trim(lines[i])) do intro[#intro + 1] = trim(lines[i]) i = i + 1 end if #intro > 0 then root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-glider-desc'):wikitext(coloured(table.concat(intro, ' '))) end local stats = root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-glider-stats') for j = i, #lines do local l = trim(lines[j]) if l ~= '' then local label, value = l:match('^(Special Skills?:)%s*(.*)$') if label then stats:wikitext(skillRow(frame, label, value, apiIds)) else -- "Special Note: Press S or ... longer. Fly in stealth for 3 seconds when Ascending." -- The sentence after the standard note is an effect of this glider: it gets its own line. local note, rest = l:match('^(Special Note:%s*Press S[^%.]*%.)%s+(%S.*)$') if note then stats:tag('div'):wikitext(coloured(note)) stats:tag('div'):wikitext(coloured(rest)) else stats:tag('div'):wikitext(coloured(l)) end end end end root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-glider-label'):wikitext('Use:') root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-glider-green'):wikitext(esc(use)) root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-glider-label'):wikitext('Equip effect') root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-glider-green'):wikitext("You can't carry another trade pack.") return tostring(root) end return p

Puts everything you give it next to each other in a row. When there is no more room the boxes continue on the next row. Any number of boxes works, there is no limit. Usage {{Div|em=0.5|first box|second box|third box}} Is the same as
first box
second box
third box
Every unnamed parameter becomes one box, in the order you write them. em (optional): the space between the boxes, in em. The default is 0.5. Empty parameters are skipped. Example {{Div|em=1|{{Mount|9002249}}|{{Mount|9002253}}|{{Mount|9002257}}}} Good to know A parameter that contains an equals sign directly in the text (for example style="color:red" in plain HTML) is read as a named parameter and disappears. Write the number in front: {{Div|1=text|2=second}}. Templates such as {{Mount|9002335|float=right}} are fine without numbers. Needs Module:Div. No description. Template parameters Parameter Description Type Status Gap em The space between the boxes, in em. Default 0.5 Default 0.5 Number optional Box 1 1 Content of the first box Content optional Box 2 2 Content of the second box Content optional Box 3 3 Content of the third box Content optional Box 4 4 Content of the fourth box. Keep adding 5, 6, 7 ... as needed, there is no limit. Content optional Box 5 5 no description Content optional Box 6 6 no description Content optional Box 7 7 no description Content optional Box 8 8 no description Content optional Box 9 9 no description Content optional Box 10 10 no description Content optional

local p = {} -- {{Div|em=0.5|first|second|third|...}} -> a flex row of <div>s that wraps when it is too wide. -- Reads the arguments of the template that called it, so there is no limit on how many you give. function p.row(frame) local args = frame:getParent().args -- gap between the boxes, in em (default 0.5) local gap = tonumber(mw.text.trim(args.em or '')) if not gap or gap < 0 then gap = 0.5 end -- collect the numbered arguments in order (1, 2, 3 ...) local keys = {} for k in pairs(args) do if type(k) == 'number' then keys[#keys + 1] = k end end table.sort(keys) local root = mw.html.create('div') :css('display', 'flex') :css('gap', gap .. 'em') :css('flex-wrap', 'wrap') local any = false for _, k in ipairs(keys) do local v = args[k] if mw.text.trim(v) ~= '' then -- empty arguments do not make an empty box root:tag('div'):wikitext(v) any = true end end if not any then return '' end return tostring(root) end return p

Row template for Template:Glider. One call per skill in the glider API, filled in by External Data (#display_external_table). It hands the skill ID and name to Module:Glider as one line of text ("id¦name‖"). Not meant to be used on its own.

local p = {} -- Reads the data that sync_wiki_data.py stored on the wiki (Module:Data/<Kind>/<number>) so the templates -- do not have to ask the APIs again and again. local IconName = require('Module:IconName') -- How many IDs share one data page. KEEP THIS IN SYNC with SHARD in sync_wiki_data.py local SHARD = { Mounts = 100, Gliders = 100, Skills = 1000, Items = 1000, Recipes = 100, Cards = 100, Pets = 100, SkillCards = 100, Buffs = 100 } local function trim(s) return mw.text.trim(tostring(s or '')) end local function esc(s) return mw.text.encode(tostring(s or ''), '<>&"\'%[%]{}|') end local loaded = {} -- One stored entry, or nil when it is not stored (yet) function p.get(kind, id) id = tonumber(id) local size = SHARD[kind] if not id or not size then return nil end id = math.floor(id) local key = kind .. '/' .. math.floor(id / size) if loaded[key] == nil then local ok, data = pcall(require, 'Module:Data/' .. key) loaded[key] = (ok and type(data) == 'table') and data or false end local data = loaded[key] return data and data[id] or nil end -- {{#invoke:DataStore|has|Mounts|8001101}} -> "1" when the data is stored, otherwise nothing function p.has(frame) return p.get(trim(frame.args[1]), frame.args[2]) and '1' or '' end -- An item by ID, for {{Item|ItemID=...}}: icon with grade border, name in the grade colour, amount. -- Args: id, amount (optional), grade (optional, replaces the item's own grade) function p.item(frame) local a = frame.args local d = p.get('Items', a.id) if not d or trim(d.name) == '' then return '' end local grade = trim(a.grade) if grade == '' then grade = trim(d.grade) end if grade == '' or grade == 'None' or grade == 'Any' then grade = 'Basic' end local out = IconName.icon({ args = { d.name, grade, size = tonumber(a.size) or 22, file = d.icon or '', over = d.over or '' } }) .. ' ' .. frame:expandTemplate{ title = 'Grade', args = { grade, esc(d.name) } } local amount = trim(a.amount) if amount ~= '' then out = out .. ' × ' .. esc(amount) end return out end return p

local p = {} -- The recipe card (the look of the item / skill cards) built from the data stored on the wiki (sync_wiki_data.py), so the crafting API is not -- asked on every page view. Only the Recipe Cost (it follows the market) comes live: Template:RecipeBox -- sends it in the argument "cost". local IconName = require('Module:IconName') local Store = require('Module:DataStore') local Tooltip = require('Module:Tooltip') -- stored() and flat(), for the hover cards local function trim(s) return mw.text.trim(tostring(s or '')) end local function esc(s) return mw.text.encode(tostring(s or ''), '<>&"\'%[%]{}|') end -- Where the box sits on the page (float parameter), inline style local STYLES = { right = 'float:right; clear:right; margin:0 0 0.5em 1em;', left = 'float:left; clear:left; margin:0 1em 0.5em 0;', center = 'width:fit-content; max-width:100%; margin:0.5em auto;', } local function num(n) n = tonumber(n) if not n then return '' end if n == math.floor(n) then return string.format('%d', n) end return tostring(n) end -- Icon with border, name in the grade colour, amount (what Template:Item shows) local function itemHtml(frame, name, grade, amount, icon, over) grade = trim(grade) if grade == '' or grade == 'None' or grade == 'Any' then grade = 'Basic' end local out = IconName.icon({ args = { name, grade, file = icon or '', over = over or '' } }) .. ' ' .. frame:expandTemplate{ title = 'Grade', args = { grade, esc(name) } } if amount and amount ~= '' then out = out .. ' × ' .. esc(amount) end return out end local function coins(frame, copper) return frame:expandTemplate{ title = 'Coins', args = { num(copper) } } end -- Hover card of an item: the tooltip card ({{Tooltip}}) in the hidden box that Template:Item/styles.css opens on hover. -- Only for items whose card data is stored (no live requests). left = the card opens to the left. local function hoverWrap(frame, inner, id, left, extraClass) id = tonumber(id) if not id or Tooltip.stored({ args = { id } }) == '' then return '' .. inner .. '' end local card = Tooltip.flat({ args = { frame:expandTemplate{ title = 'Tooltip', args = { id } } } }) return '' .. inner .. '' .. card .. '' end function p.box(frame) local a = frame.args local r = Store.get('Recipes', a.id) if not r or not r.product then return '' end local float = trim(a.float):lower() local style = STYLES[float] or 'margin:0.5em 0;' -- a box on the right side opens the hover cards to the left, so they stay on the screen local left = float == 'right' local root = mw.html.create('div'):addClass('aa-recipebox aa-rb') if float == 'right' or float == 'left' then root:addClass('aa-recipebox-float') end root:attr('style', style) -- the styles of the hover cards of the items root:wikitext(frame:extensionTag{ name = 'templatestyles', args = { src = 'Template:Item/styles.css' } }) -- header: the product (icon, name, grade; hover = its card) and the chance for 2x local prod = r.product local grade = trim(prod.grade) local hasGrade = not (grade == '' or grade == 'None' or grade == 'Any') local pgrade = hasGrade and grade or 'Basic' local head = root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-rb-head') local title = mw.html.create('span'):addClass('aa-rb-title') title:tag('span'):addClass('aa-rb-kind'):wikitext('Recipe') local name = frame:expandTemplate{ title = 'Grade', args = { pgrade, esc(prod.name) } } local amount = tonumber(prod.amount) if amount and amount > 1 then name = name .. ' × ' .. num(amount) end title:tag('span'):addClass('aa-rb-name'):wikitext(name) if hasGrade then title:tag('span'):addClass('aa-rb-grade'):wikitext(frame:expandTemplate{ title = 'Grade', args = { grade, esc(grade) } }) end local icon = IconName.icon({ args = { prod.name, pgrade, size = 48, file = prod.icon or '', over = prod.over or '' } }) head:wikitext(hoverWrap(frame, '' .. icon .. '' .. tostring(title), prod.id, left, 'aa-rb-prod')) -- "Chance for 2x": the data says 100 + the extra percent; 10000 and the like are another scale local rate = tonumber(r.rate) if rate and rate > 100 and rate < 1000 then local chip = head:tag('span'):addClass('aa-rb-chip') chip:tag('span'):addClass('aa-rb-chiplabel'):wikitext('Chance for 2x') chip:wikitext(num(math.floor((rate - 100) * 10 + 0.5) / 10) .. '%') end root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-rb-sep') -- Labor and Proficiency share the first line, the Workbench gets the line below local stats = root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-rb-stats') local function stat(row, label, value, class) local cell = row:tag('div') cell:tag('div'):addClass('aa-rb-label'):wikitext(label) cell:tag('div'):addClass('aa-rb-value' .. (class and (' ' .. class) or '')):wikitext(value) end local row1 = stats:tag('div'):addClass('aa-rb-statrow') if r.labor then stat(row1, 'Labor', num(r.labor), 'aa-rb-labor') end if r.prof then local text = esc(r.prof) local req = tonumber(r.req) if req and req ~= 0 then text = text .. ' ' .. mw.language.getContentLanguage():formatNum(req) end stat(row1, 'Proficiency', text) end if r.station then stat(stats:tag('div'):addClass('aa-rb-statrow'), 'Workbench', esc(r.station)) end root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-rb-sep') -- the materials: item (icon, name, hover card) and the amount in a column of its own root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-rb-label aa-rb-mats'):wikitext('Materials') local list = root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-rb-list') for _, m in ipairs(r.materials or {}) do local g = trim(m.required) if g == '' or g == 'Any' then g = m.grade or '' end local line = list:tag('div'):addClass('aa-rb-row') local item if m.id and Store.get('Items', m.id) then item = frame:expandTemplate{ title = 'Item', args = { ItemID = m.id, grade = g, size = 32, tip = left and 'left' or '' } } else item = itemHtml(frame, m.name, g, nil, m.icon, m.over) end line:tag('span'):addClass('aa-rb-item'):wikitext(item) line:tag('span'):addClass('aa-rb-amount'):wikitext('× ' .. num(m.amount)) end local coin = tonumber(r.coin) if coin and coin > 0 then local line = list:tag('div'):addClass('aa-rb-row') line:tag('span'):addClass('aa-rb-item aa-rb-coinlabel'):wikitext('[[File:Gold.png|24px|link=]] Coins') line:tag('span'):addClass('aa-rb-amount'):wikitext(coins(frame, coin)) end -- live from the market; a failed request leaves an error text, then there is no footer local cost = trim(a.cost) if not cost:find('class="error"', 1, true) then cost = tonumber(cost) if cost and cost > 0 then root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-rb-sep') local foot = root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-rb-foot') local lab = foot:tag('span') lab:tag('span'):addClass('aa-rb-costlabel'):wikitext('[https://sermeatball.com/tools/crafting/' .. trim(a.id) .. ' Recipe Cost]') lab:tag('span'):addClass('aa-rb-note'):wikitext('follows the market') foot:tag('span'):addClass('aa-rb-cost'):wikitext(coins(frame, cost)) end end return tostring(root) end return p

Shows the in-game style tooltip card of any item. The template finds out what kind of item it is from the item ID and uses the right card: Template:Mount for mounts, Template:Glider for gliders and Magithopters, and Template:Consumable for everything else (potions, food, talismans, tokens, crates ...). Usage {{Tooltip|9002466}} The only required parameter is the item ID. The kind of item is read from the data stored by sync_wiki_data.py (Module:Data/Cards/...). An ID that is not stored yet is looked up live (one request to the API) until the script has been run. float (optional): right, left or center, passed on to the card. speed (optional): only used by mounts, replaces the speed from the API. use (optional): replaces the "Use:" text of the card (gliders and consumables). source (optional): extra lines for the "Obtained from" part of the card (consumables and all other item cards), separated by ;;; source=no hides that part. A new card type is added in Module:Tooltip: one line in the table REGISTRY (category of the item → template). Needs Module:Tooltip, Module:DataStore and the card templates. Examples {{Tooltip|9002466}} {{Tooltip|8001101|float=right}} {{Tooltip|36793}} No description. Template parameters Parameter Description Type Status Item ID 1 The item ID, for example 9002466 Number required Position float Optional. Where the card sits on the page: right or left (text flows around it) or center. Leave empty for a normal card in the flow of the page. Suggested values right left center String optional Speed (mounts) speed Optional. Only for mounts: replaces the speed from the API. String optional Use text use Optional. Replaces the "Use:" text of the card (gliders and consumables). String optional

local p = {} -- Picks the card template for an item ID. Used by Template:Tooltip. local Store = require('Module:DataStore') -- NEW CARD TYPE = one line here: the category of the item (category_name in the API) -> the template that shows it. -- Every category that is not listed uses DEFAULT. local REGISTRY = { Mount = 'Mount', ['Marine Mount'] = 'Mount', Glider = 'Glider', Pets = 'Pet', ['Powerstone Pet'] = 'Pet', ['Battle Pet'] = 'Pet', -- Potion = 'Consumable', (listed only as an example, DEFAULT already covers it) } local DEFAULT = 'Consumable' local function trim(s) return mw.text.trim(tostring(s or '')) end -- The category of an item, when the sync script has stored it (nil when not) local function stored(id) local c = Store.get('Cards', id) if c and trim(c.category) ~= '' then return trim(c.category) end if Store.get('Mounts', id) then return 'Mount' end if Store.get('Gliders', id) then return 'Glider' end if Store.get('Pets', id) then return 'Pets' end return nil end -- {{#invoke:Tooltip|stored|ID}} -> "1" when the category is known from the stored data, otherwise nothing function p.stored(frame) return stored(frame.args[1]) and '1' or '' end -- {{#invoke:Tooltip|template|id=ID|live=}} -> name of the card template function p.template(frame) local a = frame.args local cat = stored(a.id) if not cat then cat = trim(a.live) if cat:find('class="error"', 1, true) then cat = '' end end return REGISTRY[cat] or DEFAULT end -- {{#invoke:Tooltip|flat|}}: makes a tooltip card safe to hang in the middle of a line of text -- (Template:Item, SkillLink, BuffLink). A card is built from
elements, and the browser closes the -- paragraph of the line at the first
: that leaves empty paragraphs (big gaps) between the items of a line. -- So the card is rewritten here: line breaks become spaces, and every
becomes a that looks the same: -- a div whose classes have a display rule of their own in the card styles keeps that rule, every other div -- gets display:block. When a card style gets a new class with a display rule (flex, grid, none ...), add the -- class to OWN_DISPLAY, otherwise that element is shown as a plain block. local OWN_DISPLAY = { ['aa-buff-head'] = true, ['aa-buff-title'] = true, -- Template:BuffLink/styles.css ['aa-glider'] = true, ['aa-glider-head'] = true, ['aa-glider-skillrow'] = true, ['aa-glider-skills'] = true, ['aa-glider-title'] = true, ['aa-item'] = true, ['aa-item-head'] = true, ['aa-item-title'] = true, ['aa-mount'] = true, ['aa-mount-head'] = true, ['aa-mount-title'] = true, ['aa-mskill'] = true, ['aa-mskill-effect'] = true, ['aa-mskill-head'] = true, ['aa-mskill-icon'] = true, ['aa-mskill-meta'] = true, ['aa-mskill-metaline'] = true, ['aa-mskill-name'] = true, ['aa-mskill-none'] = true, ['aa-mskill-tip'] = true, ['aa-skill'] = true, ['aa-skill-anchor'] = true, ['aa-skill-applier'] = true, ['aa-skill-applyneed'] = true, ['aa-skill-applyrow'] = true, ['aa-skill-applysub'] = true, ['aa-skill-boost'] = true, ['aa-skill-buff'] = true, ['aa-skill-buffname'] = true, ['aa-skill-bufftip'] = true, ['aa-skill-chain'] = true, ['aa-skill-chainlabel'] = true, ['aa-skill-combo'] = true, ['aa-skill-comboicons'] = true, ['aa-skill-fact'] = true, ['aa-skill-head'] = true, ['aa-skill-req'] = true, ['aa-skill-reqnote'] = true, ['aa-skill-set'] = true, ['aa-skill-step'] = true, ['aa-skill-stepicon'] = true, ['aa-skill-title'] = true, ['aa-src-head'] = true, ['aa-src-all'] = true, -- "Obtained from" part of Template:Consumable/styles.css ['aa-varmain'] = true, ['aa-varset'] = true, ['aa-varset-v1'] = true, ['aa-varset-v2'] = true, ['aa-varset-v3'] = true, ['aa-varset-v4'] = true, ['aa-varset-v5'] = true, ['aa-varset-v6'] = true, } local function divToSpan(attrs) attrs = attrs or '' local own = false local cls = attrs:match('class="([^"]*)"') if cls then for c in cls:gmatch('%S+') do if OWN_DISPLAY[c] then own = true end end end if not own then if attrs:find('style="', 1, true) then attrs = attrs:gsub('style="', 'style="display:block; ', 1) else attrs = attrs .. ' style="display:block"' end end return '' end function p.flat(frame) local s = tostring(frame.args[1] or '') s = s:gsub('%s*\n%s*', ' ') s = s:gsub(']*)>', divToSpan) s = s:gsub('
', '') return s end return p

Shows an in-game style tooltip for an item that is used or opened: potions, food, talismans, tokens, crates and so on. It is also the card for every item that has no card of its own. Normally you use Template:Tooltip, which picks the right card for any item ID. Usage {{Consumable|9002463}} The only required parameter is the item ID. The data is read from data pages stored on the wiki (Module:Data/Cards/..., made by sync_wiki_data.py). An item that is not stored yet is read live from the APIs until the script has been run for it. The card shows the category (Potion, Food, Token ...), the grade, the name, "Untradeable" for bound items, the description, and the "Use:" effect, with the colours of the game. float (optional): right or left places the card at that side with the text flowing around it, center centres it. use (optional): replaces the "Use:" text. source (optional): extra lines for the "Obtained from" part at the end of the card, separated by ;;. The crafts and quests that give the item are added automatically from the stored data, with every quest linking to the aa-classic.com quest database; lines that belong to the item itself are typed on Module:Data/Sources. source=no hides the whole part. untradeable (optional): no hides the "Untradeable" line (the pet card uses this when it falls back to this card). Needs Module:Consumable, Module:IconName, Module:DataStore, Template:Grade and Template:Consumable/styles.css. Examples {{Consumable|9002463}} {{Consumable|9002466|float=right}} No description. Template parameters Parameter Description Type Status Item ID 1 The item ID, for example 9002463 Number required Position float Optional. Where the card sits on the page: right or left (text flows around it) or center. Leave empty for a normal card in the flow of the page. Suggested values right left center String optional Use text use Optional. Replaces the "Use:" text of the card. String optional Show Untradeable untradeable Optional. Write no to hide the "Untradeable" line. Suggested values no String optional

local p = {} -- In-game style card for items that are used up or opened: potions, food, talismans, tokens, crates and -- every other item that has no card of its own. The category label (Potion, Food ...) comes from the API. local IconName = require('Module:IconName') local Store = require('Module:DataStore') -- data stored on the wiki by sync_wiki_data.py local function trim(s) return mw.text.trim(tostring(s or '')) end local function esc(s) return mw.text.encode(tostring(s or ''), '<>&"'%[%]{}|') end -- Colours of the game's short codes: |nc;...|r is orange, |ni;...|r is yellow, |nd;...|r is light blue ("loot drop rate"). Others show without colour. local NCODE = { c = 'FF9C27', i = 'F5CB65', d = 'A3E3FD' } -- The game marks highlighted words as |cFFRRGGBB...|r; only those parts get a colour. -- A coloured part may run over several lines: every line gets its own span, so lines can be split afterwards. local function coloured(text, hook) text = tostring(text or '') -- hook(code, inner) may return ready HTML for a |nX;...|r part (the pet card puts hoverable skills there) local toks = {} text = text:gsub('|n(%a);(.-)|r', function(code, inner) if hook then local h = hook(code, inner) if h then toks[#toks + 1] = h return '\1' .. #toks .. '\2' end end if NCODE[code] then return '|cFF' .. NCODE[code] .. inner .. '|r' end return inner end) local out, pos = {}, 1 while true do local s, e, rgb, inner = text:find('|c%x%x(%x%x%x%x%x%x)(.-)|r', pos) if not s then break end out[#out + 1] = esc(text:sub(pos, s - 1)) local parts = {} for _, seg in ipairs(mw.text.split(inner, ' ', true)) do if mw.text.trim(seg) == '' then parts[#parts + 1] = seg else parts[#parts + 1] = '' .. esc(seg) .. '' end end out[#out + 1] = table.concat(parts, ' ') pos = e + 1 end out[#out + 1] = esc(text:sub(pos)) local html = table.concat(out) if #toks > 0 then html = html:gsub('\1(%d+)\2', function(i) return toks[tonumber(i)] end) end return html end -- Where the card sits on the page (float parameter), set inline so it works without the style page local FLOATS = { right = 'float:right; clear:right; margin:0 0 0.5em 1em;', left = 'float:left; clear:left; margin:0 1em 0.5em 0;', center = 'margin:0 auto 0.5em auto;', } -- Binding of the item (bind_type of the API). "normal" shows nothing. local BIND = { soulbound_pickup = 'Untradeable', soulbound_unpack = 'Untradeable', soulbound_equip = 'Binds when equipped', } -- "-@ITEM_NAME(38620)" in a description is the name of that item local function names(text) return (text:gsub('@ITEM_NAME%((%d+)%)', function(id) local it = Store.get('Items', id) or Store.get('Cards', id) return it and trim(it.name) ~= '' and trim(it.name) or ('Item ' .. id) end)) end -- Text with line breaks: every line its own row, a blank line leaves some space local function paragraphs(text, class, hook) text = trim(names(tostring(text or ''):gsub(' ', ''))) if text == '' then return nil end local box = mw.html.create('div'):addClass(class) local gap = false for _, line in ipairs(mw.text.split(coloured(text, hook), ' ', true)) do line = trim(line) if line == '' then gap = true else local row = box:tag('div'):wikitext(line) if gap then row:addClass('aa-item-gap') end gap = false end end return box end local function fetched(s) s = trim(s) if s:find('class="error"', 1, true) then return '' end return s end -- shared with Module:Skill p.paragraphs = paragraphs -- ---- "Obtained from": crafts and quests that give the item (stored by sync_wiki_data.py) and the lines that editors type in ---- local SHOW = 5 -- entries of a group that are shown in the card; the whole list opens when the pointer rests on "and N more" local QUEST_URL = 'https://aa-classic.com/database/quests/' local CRAFT_URL = 'https://sermeatball.com/tools/crafting/' -- The lines typed in by editors: the data page Module:Data/Sources (one entry per item ID) and the source= parameter -- of the template (lines separated by ;;) local function typedLines(id, param) local lines = {} local ok, data = pcall(require, 'Module:Data/Sources') if ok and type(data) == 'table' then local e = data[tonumber(id)] if type(e) == 'string' then e = { e } end if type(e) == 'table' then for _, t in ipairs(e) do if trim(t) ~= '' then lines[#lines + 1] = trim(t) end end end end for part in (tostring(param or '') .. ';;'):gmatch('(.-);;') do part = trim(part) if part ~= '' then lines[#lines + 1] = part end end return lines end local function sourceLine(parent, class, url, row) parent:tag('div'):addClass('aa-src-line ' .. class) :wikitext('[' .. url .. tostring(row[1]) .. ' ' .. esc(row[2]) .. ']') end -- One group (Crafting, Quest rewards): the first SHOW entries, then "and N more" that opens the whole list local function sourceGroup(root, title, rows, class, url) if type(rows) ~= 'table' or #rows == 0 then return end local g = root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-src-group') local head = g:tag('div'):addClass('aa-src-head') head:tag('span'):addClass('aa-src-name'):wikitext(title .. (#rows > 1 and (' (' .. #rows .. ')') or '')) for i = 1, math.min(SHOW, #rows) do sourceLine(g, class, url, rows[i]) end if #rows > SHOW then local more = g:tag('div'):addClass('aa-src-more') more:tag('span'):addClass('aa-src-morelabel'):wikitext('and ' .. (#rows - SHOW) .. ' more') local box = more:tag('div'):addClass('aa-src-all'):tag('div'):addClass('aa-src-box') box:tag('div'):addClass('aa-src-boxhead'):wikitext(title .. ' (' .. #rows .. ')') for _, r in ipairs(rows) do sourceLine(box, class, url, r) end end end local function sourcesPart(root, d, opts) if trim(opts.source):lower() == 'no' then return end local typed = typedLines(opts.id, opts.source) local hasCraft = type(d.crafts) == 'table' and #d.crafts > 0 local hasQuest = type(d.quests) == 'table' and #d.quests > 0 if not (hasCraft or hasQuest or #typed > 0) then return end root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-item-sep') local box = root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-src') box:tag('div'):addClass('aa-src-title'):wikitext('Obtained from') sourceGroup(box, 'Crafting', d.crafts, 'aa-src-craft', CRAFT_URL) sourceGroup(box, 'Quest rewards', d.quests, 'aa-src-quest', QUEST_URL) if #typed > 0 then local g = box:tag('div'):addClass('aa-src-group') g:tag('div'):addClass('aa-src-head'):tag('span'):addClass('aa-src-name'):wikitext('Other') for _, t in ipairs(typed) do g:tag('div'):addClass('aa-src-line aa-src-other'):wikitext(t) end end end -- The card from ready data d = { name, grade, category, icon, over, desc, use, bind, req } -- opts: float, hook (see coloured), use (replaces the Use text), bind (true = show "Untradeable" with a line under it), -- sources (true = the "Obtained from" part, only Template:Consumable asks for it), id, source (lines typed in the template) function p.render(frame, d, opts) opts = opts or {} local name = trim(d.name) local grade = trim(d.grade) local hasGrade = not (grade == '' or grade == 'None' or grade == 'Any') if not hasGrade then grade = 'Basic' end -- no grade: Basic look, and no grade line local category = trim(d.category) local use = trim(opts.use) if use == '' then use = trim(d.use) end local bind = BIND[trim(d.bind)] local float = trim(opts.float):lower() if not FLOATS[float] then float = '' end local root = mw.html.create('div'):addClass('aa-item') if float == 'right' or float == 'left' then root:addClass('aa-item-float') end if float == 'right' then root:addClass('aa-item-right') end if float ~= '' then root:attr('style', FLOATS[float]) end -- header: icon, category, grade, name local head = root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-item-head') head:tag('div'):addClass('aa-item-icon'):wikitext(IconName.icon({ args = { name, grade, size = 48, file = d.icon, over = d.over } })) local title = head:tag('div'):addClass('aa-item-title') if category ~= '' then title:tag('div'):addClass('aa-item-cat'):wikitext(esc(category)) end if hasGrade then title:tag('div'):addClass('aa-item-grade'):wikitext( frame:expandTemplate{ title = 'Grade', args = { grade, esc(grade) } }) end title:tag('div'):addClass('aa-item-name'):wikitext( frame:expandTemplate{ title = 'Grade', args = { grade, esc(name) } }) root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-item-sep') -- "Untradeable" only where the card asks for it (opts.bind); the required level is not shown if bind and opts.bind then root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-item-line'):wikitext(esc(bind)) root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-item-sep') -- the line that separates "Untradeable" from the description end local body = paragraphs(d.desc, 'aa-item-desc', opts.hook) if body then root:node(body) end local useBox = paragraphs(use, 'aa-item-green') if useBox then root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-item-label'):wikitext('Use:') root:node(useBox) end if opts.sources then sourcesPart(root, d, opts) end return tostring(root) end function p.card(frame) local a = frame.args local d = Store.get('Cards', a.id) local name = d and trim(d.name) or fetched(a.name) if name == '' then return '' end local data if d then data = d else -- live data (the item is not stored yet) data = { name = name, grade = fetched(a.grade), category = fetched(a.category), icon = fetched(a.icon), over = fetched(a.over), desc = fetched(a.desc), use = fetched(a.cuse), bind = fetched(a.bind), req = fetched(a.req) } end return p.render(frame, data, { float = a.float, use = a.use, bind = trim(a.untradeable):lower() ~= 'no', sources = true, id = a.id, source = a.source }) end return p

Normally you use Template:Tooltip, which picks the right card for any item ID. Usage {{Pet|56039}} The only required parameter is the item ID of the pet (the item, not the NPC). A pet that is not stored yet is shown as a plain card (Template:Consumable, read live) without the skill boxes until the script has been run for it. float (optional): right or left places the card at that side with the text flowing around it, center centres it. use (optional): replaces the "Use:" text. Needs Module:Pet, Module:Consumable, Module:Mount (for the hover box), Module:DataStore, Template:Consumable, Template:Consumable/styles.css and Template:Mount/styles.css. Data: Module:Data/Pets/..., made by -- sync_wiki_data.py; the skills' details come from Module:Data/Skills/... local Consumable = require('Module:Consumable') local Store = require('Module:DataStore') local Mount = require('Module:Mount') -- its hover box for a skill local function trim(s) return mw.text.trim(tostring(s or '')) end -- "Relaxed Life" and "relaxed life!" are the same skill local function key(s) return (tostring(s or ''):lower():gsub('[^%a%d]', '')) end -- {{#invoke:Pet|card|id=56039|float=|use=}} (nothing when the pet is not stored) function p.card(frame) local a = frame.args local d = Store.get('Pets', a.id) if not d or trim(d.name) == '' then return '' end local byName = {} for _, s in ipairs(d.skills or {}) do if s.name then byName[key(s.name)] = s end end -- the game writes the skill names as |nd;Name|r (light blue): those become hover boxes local function hook(code, inner) if code ~= 'd' then return nil end local s = byName[key(inner)] if not s then return nil end local sk = Store.get('Skills', s.id) or {} local html = Mount.hover({ args = { name = trim(inner), realname = sk.name or s.name or '', color = 'A3E3FD', cd = sk.cd or '', cast = sk.cast or '', mana = sk.mana and tostring(sk.mana) or '', desc = (sk.desc or s.desc or ''):gsub('\r', ''), icon = sk.icon or s.icon or '', } }) return (html:gsub('\n', ' ')) end return Consumable.render(frame, d, { float = a.float, use = a.use, hook = hook }) end return p

Shows an in-game style tooltip card for a skill: icon, skill line, name, element (top right), rank, mana, range, effect range, attack percent, cast time, cooldown, the effects it grants (buff icons), the description with the damage formula, combos and the chain the skill belongs to. This is a card you place on a page. The hover boxes of mount, glider and pet skills are separate and are not changed by this template. Usage {{Skill|36597}} The only required parameter is the skill ID (the number at the end of https://aa-classic.com/database/skills/36597). Skill IDs are not item IDs. The data is read from data pages stored on the wiki (Module:Data/SkillCards/..., made by sync_wiki_data.py). A skill that is not stored yet is read live from the API (without the effect icons) until the script has been run for it. Mana, range, effect range, cast time, cooldown, channeling time and labor cost are only shown when the data has them. The mana cost of many skills is calculated by the game and is 0 in the data, so no Mana line is shown then. Versions: a skill with ancestral versions (Flamebolt: Basic, Flame, Lightning) lists them at the top right of the card, the shown one in gold. Clicking another name shows that version with its own description, effects, combos and chain (the same step of the chain is kept if the version has one). Rank (after the name, Triple Slash (Rank 1)) comes from the ancestral skill data. The versions are stored by sync_wiki_data.py together with the skill; each version can have its own card size, only the cards of one chain keep the same size. Damage: the game's #{avg_damage} in the description is replaced by the formula of the data in green, for example (260% Melee Attack), and the line Melee Attack +260% is shown under the ranges. The final damage is not calculated, because it depends on gear, level and conditions in the game. Combo: the sentences of the game with the icon of the condition and the result. Chain: skills that follow each other (Triple Slash) show all steps with the icons, the skill of the card is outlined. Clicking another icon switches the card to that skill, there is no need to put each skill on the page. The chain is found automatically from the data, and all skills of a chain are stored by sync_wiki_data.py when one of them is. The switching uses a link to the card (the address gets #aa-skill36405-v1k2 added) and CSS, so it also works for readers without scripts. All of this needs the skill to be stored (sync_wiki_data.py). A skill that is not stored yet is shown from the live API with the basic lines only. float (optional): right or left places the card at that side with the text flowing around it, center centres it. The icons need to be uploaded: upload_icons_by_api.py --kind skills and --kind buffs (effect and combo icons). Needs Module:Skill, Module:Consumable, Module:IconName, Module:DataStore and Template:Skill/styles.css. Examples {{Skill|36597}} {{Skill|36597|float=right}} No description. Template parameters Parameter Description Type Status Skill ID 1 The skill ID, for example 36597 Number required Position float Optional. Where the card sits on the page: right or left (text flows around it) or center. Leave empty for a normal card in the flow of the page. Suggested values right left center String optional

Data: Module:Data/SkillCards/... 'min' end if s > 0 or m == 0 then out[#out + 1] = n(s) .. 'sec' end return table.concat(out, ' ') end -- Unfilled placeholders of the game text. #{avg_damage}#{detail_melee_damage} (two in a row) is the damage: the game -- shows "2180 (0 + 267% Melee Attack)", here the formula "(260% Melee Attack)" in green. ')|r' end -- a total that is not the damage formula (damage over time of a buff): the number is not known return '(varies)' end)) end -- 260 -> "260", 0.5 -> "0.5" local function g(x) x = tonumber(x) or 0 if x == math.floor(x) then return string.format('%d', x) end return (string.format('%.2f', x):gsub('0+$', '')) end -- the damage formula as the data gives it: "0 + 260% Melee Attack" or "18-30 + 290% Melee Attack" local function formula(list) local parts = {} for _, x in ipairs(type(list) == 'table' and list or {}) do local text = g(x.pct) .. '-' .. g(x.fmax) end text = flat .. ' + ' .. text end if x.lvl then text = text .. ', scales with level' end parts[#parts + 1] = text end if #parts == 0 then return nil end return table.concat(parts, ' + ') end -- small icon of the wiki (an effect, a skill) local function pic(icon, size) local f = IconName.iconFile(icon) if f == '' then return '' end return '[[File:' .. f .. '|' .. size .. 'px|link=]]' end -- 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th ... 11th, 21st local function ordinal(i) local last, teen = i % 10, i % 100 local suffix = 'th' if teen < 11 or teen > 13 then suffix = (last == 1 and 'st') or (last == 2 and 'nd') or (last == 3 and 'rd') or 'th' end return i .. suffix end -- data of the card: stored, or built from the live arguments of Template:Skill local function data(a) local d = Store.get('SkillCards', a.id) if d then return d end local name = fetched(a.name) if name == '' then return nil end return { name = name, icon = fetched(a.icon), line = fetched(a.line), desc = fetched(a.desc), cd = num(fetched(a.cd)), cast = num(fetched(a.cast)), mana = num(fetched(a.mana)), minr = num(fetched(a.minr)), maxr = num(fetched(a.maxr)), rad = num(fetched(a.rad)), labor = num(fetched(a.labor)) } end -- one line of the box local function line(root, class, text) root:tag('div'):addClass(class):wikitext(text) end -- Effects with ranks (Magic Circle Rank 1 ... A rank that does not exist: the closest lower one. local function ranked(buffs, want) local t = tonumber(want) or 1 local function score(r) if r <= t then return t - r end return 1000 + (r - t) end local out, pos = {}, {} for _, b in ipairs(type(buffs) == 'table' and buffs or {}) do if not tonumber(b.rk) then out[#out + 1] = b else local key = tostring(b.icon) .. ')' end title:tag('div'):addClass('aa-skill-name'):wikitext(esc(name)) -- an item that raises the rank of the skill (Fantasia of Sorcery): its icon is a switch between the card and the same -- card one rank higher (rank and effect of that rank); left of the versions, so those stay where they are if ctx.boostBtn and IconName.iconFile(ctx.boostBtn.item.icon) ~= '' then local bb = ctx.boostBtn local plus = tonumber(bb.item.plus) or 1 local btn = head:tag('div'):addClass('aa-skill-boost') if bb.on then btn:addClass('aa-skill-boost-on') end btn:wikitext('[[File:' .. The skill tree window of the game for one tree: the combat skills, the passives and (a click on the eye) the Abyssal skills. Hover a skill to see its card, a passive to see its text. Everything is shown for a player of level 55. Usage {{Skilltree|Sorcery}} {{Skilltree|Sorcery|abyssal=yes}} {{Skilltree|Sorcery|float=right}} The boxes of the skills open to the right of the tree. In a tree on the right of the page (float=right) they open to the left; tips=left or tips=right sets it by hand. A box shows the skill with the rank of the game screenshots; its versions (Basic, Quake ...) and the skills of its chain can be switched inside the box.Needs Module:Skilltree, Module:Skilltree/data, Template:Skilltree/styles.css (this template) and Template:Skill/styles.css, Module:Skill (the cards) File:Ability_change.png (the eye icon is cut out of it) The icons of the skills and of the passives (buff icons), uploaded like for Template:Tl No description. Template parameters Parameter Description Type Status Skill tree 1 The name of the tree, for example Sorcery Suggested values Sorcery String required Abyssal open abyssal yes = the Abyssal skills are shown from the start (the eye still closes them) Suggested values yes String optional Position float Optional. left, right (text flows around the tree) or center. A tree on the right opens its boxes to the left. Suggested values left right center String optional Boxes open to tips Optional. left or right; normally right, and left when float=right. Suggested values left right String optional

/* Template:Skilltree/styles.css - the skill tree window. Tiles are 60px. The cards open at the side of the tile on hover, starting halfway down the tile (so the pointer can still pass over the upper half of the next tile): to the right in a tree with .aa-tree-tips-right (a tree on the left of the page), to the left in .aa-tree-tips-left (float=right). A closed card has no size (width and height 0) so it does not widen the page. '|' .. size .. 'px|link=]]' end -- a piece of the sprite sheet (the CSS crops it) local function sprite(class) return '[[File:' .. SPRITE .. '.', 'aa-tree-ptext') rich(tip, 'Learning it costs 1 skill point.', 'aa-tree-ptext') end end -- an empty layer after the tiles of a grid: while one of the tiles is clicked open (focus) it covers the whole tree, so the -- other tiles cannot be hovered and their cards cannot open on top of the open one; a click on it closes the card local function shield(grid) grid:tag('div'):addClass('aa-tree-shield') end function p.tree(frame) local pf = frame:getParent() local a = pf and pf.args or frame.args local want = trim(a[1]):lower() local name, t for k, v in pairs(Data) do if k:lower() == want then name, t = k, v end end local styles = frame:extensionTag('templatestyles', '', { src = 'Template:Skill/styles.css' }) .. frame:extensionTag('templatestyles', '', { src = 'Template:Skilltree/styles.css' }) if not t then return styles .. '"' end local open = yes(a.abyssal) local ovs = {} -- the numbers of the skills (and of their versions) by skill id for id, c in pairs(t.cards or {}) do ovs[id] = override(c) if type(c.boost) == 'table' then ovs[id].boost = override(c.boost) end -- the numbers with the rank item (+1) end local key = name:lower():gsub('[^%w]', '') local idTop, idBottom = 'aa-abyss1-' .. key, 'aa-abyss2-' .. key local function collapsible(parent, id) local box = parent:tag('div'):addClass('mw-collapsible'):attr('id', 'mw-customcollapsible-' .. id) if not open then box:addClass('mw-collapsed') end return box end -- where the tree sits on the page (float) and so where the boxes open: to the right of a tree on the left -- of the page, to the left of a tree on the right (tips = left or right overrides it) local float = trim(a.float):lower() local tips = trim(a.tips):lower() if tips ~= 'left' and tips ~= 'right' then tips = (float == 'right') and 'left' or 'right' end local root = mw.html.create('div'):addClass('aa-tree aa-tree-tips-' .. tips) if float == 'right' then root:attr('style', 'float:right; clear:right; margin:0 0 0.5em 1em;') elseif float == 'left' then root:attr('style', 'float:left; clear:left; margin:0 1em 0.5em 0;') elseif float == 'center' then root:attr('style', 'display:table; margin:0 auto 0.5em auto;') end -- combat root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-tree-name'):wikitext(mw.text.encode(name, '<>&"\'')) local head = root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-tree-head') head:tag('span'):addClass('aa-tree-title'):wikitext('Combat') local grid = root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-tree-grid') for i, id in ipairs(t.combat) do skillTile(grid, id, (i - 1) % 4 + 1, t.ranks, ovs) end shield(grid) if t.abyssal and #t.abyssal > 0 then -- the space of the row stays when it is closed: the collapsible only hides the content wrapper inside it. ' mw-customtoggle-' .. idBottom) :attr('title', 'Abyssal skills') :wikitext(sprite('aa-eye-on') .. sprite('aa-eye-off') .. sprite('aa-eye-hover')) end -- passives root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-tree-head aa-tree-head-p'):tag('span'):addClass('aa-tree-title'):wikitext('Passive') local pg = root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-tree-grid') for i, ps in ipairs(t.passives or {}) do local col = (i - 1) % 4 + 1 local tile = pg:tag('div'):addClass('aa-tree-tile aa-tree-col' .. col):attr('tabindex', '0') tile:tag('div'):addClass('aa-tree-ico'):wikitext(icon(ps.icon, 56)) passiveTip(tile, ps, name, ps.num) end shield(pg) if t.abyssalPassive then local box = collapsible(root, idBottom):addClass('aa-tree-abp') -- the space stays when it is closed: only the content wrapper is hidden by the collapsible local g3 = box:tag('div'):addClass('mw-collapsible-content'):tag('div'):addClass('aa-tree-grid') local tile = g3:tag('div'):addClass('aa-tree-tile aa-tree-col1'):attr('tabindex', '0') tile:tag('div'):addClass('aa-tree-ico'):wikitext(icon(t.abyssalPassive.icon, 56)) passiveTip(tile, t.abyssalPassive, name, nil) shield(g3) end -- watermark at the bottom, centred root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-tree-mark'):wikitext('[[File:Favicon.png|60px|link=]]') return styles .. tostring(root) end return p

When the pointer rests on the icon or the name, the skill's tooltip card (Template:Skill) opens beside it. The icon, name and card come from the data pages stored by sync_wiki_data.py (the same pages as Template:Skill; --scan finds the SkillLink calls on the wiki). A skill that is not stored yet shows nothing (an invisible comment is left in the page source) until the script has been run. The card opens to the right of the skill (towards the middle of the page for normal text). tip=left opens it to the left instead, for skills at the right edge, for example in an infobox. tip=no turns the tooltip off. size=32 makes the icon larger (default 22, which fits in a line of text). On phones the card opens below. The colour of the name is set in Template:SkillLink/styles.css (.aa-skilltip-name). When Will the New Client Become the Default?
x: Announcement31 October 2026·All news·Original post on aa-classic.com The Road to 2.0: Part 2 — Opening the Beta The new client beta is now open to everyone! After a week of crash fixes, performance optimizations, and engine improvements, we're ready to welcome more players. Here's what's changed and what's next. Hello everyone, Aguru here! It's been almost a week since we introduced our new game client in the first part of our Road to 2.0 series, and quite a lot has happened since then! We've been working alongside our closed beta testers, fixing crashes, improving performance, and ironing out the quirks that come with modernizing an engine that's over a decade old. Today, I'd like to share some of our progress, discuss a few interesting improvements, and announce our next big step. Starting today, the new client beta is open to everyone! From Closed Beta to Open Beta Over the past several days, we've been inviting increasingly large groups of players, gathering feedback, investigating crashes, and releasing fixes at a rather ridiculous pace. Thanks to our testers, we've identified and resolved numerous issues that would have been difficult to reproduce internally. The results have been encouraging, and we're now comfortable opening the doors to everyone. As of this post, all players can opt into the new client beta directly through the launcher. The original client will remain available, and you can switch back at any time if you encounter issues. Of course, this is still a beta. There are known bugs, undoubtedly some we haven't discovered yet, and improvements that will take more time to get right. But we're making progress, and we're ready for more players to join us! What We've Fixed So Far Since the closed beta began, we've pushed numerous updates addressing everything from minor visual issues to long-standing engine crashes. Here are some of the highlights. Stability and Crash Fixes We've addressed a considerable number of crashes, including issues involving: Character selection, loading screens, and entering or leaving the world. UI initialization, addons, and character customization. Housing placement and interactions with world objects. Texture streaming and graphics resource management. Audio playback during large-scale PvP. Switching between windowed and fullscreen modes. We've also implemented initial fixes for NVIDIA-specific crashes, alongside expanded diagnostics that provide much more information when something goes wrong. These improvements make it significantly easier for us to investigate and resolve difficult issues. Not every crash is solved yet, but we're in a much better position to track them down. Performance Improvements We've made numerous optimizations throughout the engine, including: Faster shader loading and improved texture streaming. Smoother terrain and shadow rendering. Reduced stuttering when loading houses and decorations. Better performance when planting and interacting with the UI. Fixes for visual effects accumulating in memory during long sessions. While some of these improvements are small individually, together they help make the client more responsive and consistent. A Major Change to How the UI Works One of our latest updates introduces a particularly interesting change: the user interface now runs on its own thread while you're in the game world. Previously, UI processing competed with other game operations, including rendering. With this change, the UI can perform more of its work independently, potentially improving performance in raids, large-scale PvP, and crowded areas. It's a substantial architectural improvement, and a good example of what's now possible with the new client. However, it's also a new system, so we're particularly interested in reports of unusual UI behavior, incorrect tooltips, addon issues, or unexpected crashes. Gameplay and Visual Fixes Not everything has been happening behind the scenes! We've also fixed a variety of gameplay issues: Mount animations now correctly match movement direction, and water mounts no longer immediately despawn. Ladders, including boat ladders, are climbable again. Cannons should now correctly hit their targets. Ironclads, freighters, and cargo ships have received physics fixes. They should be considerably less interested in becoming spacecraft. Character statistics, proficiency limits, party indicators, and customization visuals have been corrected. Fishing rod animations and several UI issues have been fixed. Audio issues causing loud popping sounds and disappearing game audio have been addressed. Ping and latency reporting should be more accurate. We've also temporarily enabled Snap Planting, with Shift allowing you to disable snapping while placing objects. We'd love to hear your thoughts on this feature before deciding how to move forward with it. And these are only some of the fixes we've made! What's Next? Opening the beta is an important milestone, but there's still plenty of work ahead. Our priorities remain stability, performance, and compatibility, particularly as more players begin testing across different hardware configurations and gameplay situations. We'll also continue making improvements to the engine itself, much like the new UI threading system. When Will the New Client Become the Default? We don't have a confirmed date just yet. Our goal is to make the new client at least as reliable as the original, without major compatibility issues preventing players from using it. Once we're confident we've reached that point, we'll transition it into the default experience. Until then, both clients will remain available. Improving the New Player Experience Alongside our work on the new client, we've also begun focusing on another important area: the new player experience. ArcheAge is a massive game, and getting started can be overwhelming, particularly for players unfamiliar with its systems. We want to make the early stages of the game more approachable, improve how players are introduced to its various activities, and ultimately give newcomers more reasons to stick around. Improving new player retention is one of our priorities, and we believe there's plenty we can do without compromising what makes ArcheAge Classic special. We're currently aiming to deliver a major update in the coming months, alongside the final release of the new client, with a strong focus on these improvements. This remains a tentative target, and we'll share more details as development progresses. After all, a better client is only part of the equation. We also want to make ArcheAge Classic a better experience for the players joining us. We Need Your Feedback! The closed beta has demonstrated just how valuable player feedback is. Many of the issues we've fixed were identified thanks to players reporting crashes, explaining unexpected behavior, or providing reproducible examples. With the beta now open, we'd love for more of you to get involved! Whether it's a crash, visual bug, performance issue, or something that simply doesn't feel right, please report it. Including your hardware, addons, and what you were doing at the time makes a huge difference. And if everything works perfectly? We'd love to hear that too! Looking Ahead The new client was never just about replacing the old one. It was about giving ourselves the freedom to improve ArcheAge in ways that previously weren't possible. We're only beginning to take advantage of that freedom, and there's still plenty of work ahead. But the progress we've made in such a short time is encouraging, and we're excited to finally get this project into everyone's hands. The new client beta is now open. Give it a try, let us know what you think, and help us build a better ArcheAge Classic! Thank you to everyone who participated in the closed beta, and to everyone who continues to support the project. — Aguru ArcheAge Classic Team

What does this mean for players?
x: Announcement25 October 2026·All news·Original post on aa-classic.com Developer Blog: The Road to 2.0 & Beyond | Part 1 What's been happening behind the scenes at ArcheAge Classic? In this first developer blog, we take a look at our new game client, why we're rebuilding it, and how we plan to get it into players' hands Hello everyone, Aguru here! It's been quite a while since our last developer blog, and I figured it was about time for another one. Today, I'd like to give you a little insight into what we've been working on behind the scenes, particularly one of our biggest technical undertakings yet: a new game client for ArcheAge Classic. This is the first part of our Road to 2.0 series, where we'll be discussing the work leading up to our next major update and what it means for the future of ArcheAge Classic. The Road to 2.0: Part 1 — A New Client As some of you may know, we've been working towards what we've lovingly labelled 2.0, our next major update to ArcheAge Classic. However, before we get there, there's something rather important we need to talk about. For quite some time now, we've been working behind the scenes on a project that will fundamentally change what we're capable of doing with ArcheAge Classic. We're building a new game client. Why a new client? The original ArcheAge client is rather old, and over the years, we've run into countless limitations that have made development increasingly difficult. One of the biggest examples is the game's 32-bit architecture, which severely limits how much memory the client can use. This has been responsible for a considerable number of crashes, particularly during longer play sessions or when travelling between populated areas. And while we've spent a great deal of time working around these limitations, there's only so much we can do without making more fundamental changes. That's where our new client comes in. We're rebuilding and modernizing significant parts of the client, giving us far greater control over how the game works. Some of the improvements we're working towards include: 64-bit support: Removing the limitations of the original 32-bit client, allowing the game to utilize significantly more memory and reducing memory-related crashes. Performance improvements: Optimizing various parts of the engine to improve performance and reduce unnecessary overhead. Improved stability: Addressing long-standing client crashes and engine issues that were previously difficult or impossible to fix. Quality-of-life improvements: Greater freedom to implement new client-side functionality, such as alternative interaction buttons and other features that were previously out of reach. Future development: Establishing a modernized foundation that will allow us to make more substantial improvements to the game going forward. It's important to understand that this isn't a new version of ArcheAge in the traditional sense. It's not a fresh start, a new server, or a major content update. It's still the same ArcheAge Classic you know, just running on an improved foundation. And perhaps most importantly, this is not a one-off update. The new client is intended to become the foundation for all future client development. What does this mean for players? Initially, you probably won't notice a massive difference. That's intentional. Our first priority is ensuring that the new client can run the game as reliably as the existing one, while taking advantage of the improvements we've made under the hood. Some players may notice performance improvements, fewer crashes, or other small changes, but we're not trying to reinvent the game overnight. Instead, we're laying the groundwork for improvements that simply wouldn't have been feasible with the original client. The amount of control this project gives us over the game is something we've wanted for years, and we're incredibly excited about what it will allow us to do in the future. How will the rollout work? Of course, replacing the game client is not something we want to rush. The new client is currently undergoing internal testing, and our next step will be to gradually introduce it to the live player population, which will begin promptly. Rather than releasing it to everyone at once, we'll be conducting an invite-only beta directly on the live servers. Here's how it'll work: Invitations will be distributed in waves. A random selection of active players will be invited to participate, with factors such as recent playtime influencing the selection process. Invites will appear directly in the launcher. If you're selected, you'll know! There's no need to apply, sign up, or constantly check for an invitation. You won't miss it. Both clients will coexist. During the beta, the new client will run alongside the existing one. Invited players will be able to test it without us immediately replacing the old client. We'll gradually expand access. As we fix bugs, address crashes, and gain confidence in the new client, we'll increase the percentage of the player population using it. Eventually, the new client will become the official client. Once we're satisfied with its stability and overall readiness, we'll transition away from the legacy client. We fully expect there to be some rough edges during the beta. After all, we're making substantial changes to a game engine that's been around for well over a decade. That's precisely why we're taking this gradual approach. Your feedback and crash reports will be invaluable in helping us identify issues that might not appear during internal testing. We'd much rather take the time to get this right than rush everyone onto a new client before it's ready. Looking ahead Our new client represents a tremendous amount of work behind the scenes, much of which players will never directly see. But it's also one of the most important investments we can make in the future of ArcheAge Classic. For years, we've had ideas and improvements that simply weren't practical because of the limitations of the original client. With this project, we're finally starting to remove those barriers. And while the initial release will be focused primarily on stability, compatibility, and performance, the possibilities it opens up for future development are what make this project particularly exciting. This is only the beginning. In the next part of our Road to 2.0 series, we'll dive deeper into the upcoming 2.0 update itself and what we're planning for the future of AAClassic. Until then, thank you all for continuing to support us, and we look forward to getting the new client into your hands! — Aguru ArcheAge Classic Team

New Profession: Taming (Preview) Taming has been added as a new profession. Taming is the first custom profession that is being added to Archeage Classic. This profession will fall under “Special” Category and revolve around taming wild beasts out in the world, either using these as your own personal mounts, trading them with other players or exchanging them for materials used in various different crafting recipes. There are two ways to find wild beasts to tame. 1- By roaming Erenor and finding wild, wandering tameable beasts 2- By instigating tameable beasts to come out of their hiding by slaughtering their kind Almost every zone in Erenor has wild beasts to tame, so explore and catch them all! To start taming, you need a Tamer’s backpack, a simple leather-bound bag filled to the brim with crucial tools to tame beasts. Currently, there are 3 tiers of backpacks: Greenhorn’s Backpack: Requires 0 Taming proficiency to use To craft this backpack, you need: 5x Vita Seed 10x Leather 10x Apple Wrangler’s Backpack: Requires 80.000 Taming proficiency to use To craft this backpack, you need: 1x Greenhorn’s Backpack 10x Hay Bale 10x Apricot 10x Orange 10x Pomegranate 200x Whistle of the Wild (These will be explained later) Herdmaster’s Backpack: Requires 200.000 Taming proficiency to use To craft this backpack, you need: 1x Greenhorn’s Backpack 10x Royal Seed 5x Wind Spirit Leather 100x Cherry 100x Jujube 100x Coconut 600x Whistle of the Wild Taming is similar to fishing in terms of mechanics but has a little more depth. When you attempt to tame a wild beast you will notice its HP drop drastically at first. That’s your progress bar to tame the beast. The beast may display several “moods” during the taming process. React in time with the correct action and you will gain its trust and come closer to taming it. When you’ve successfully filled the beast’s HP bar, it will accept you as its new owner and you will gain a Mysterious Beast. The type of beast is determined by the creature you’ve just tamed. If it was a boar, you’ll get a Mysterious Boar. When you’ve successfully filled the beast’s HP bar, you will receive a Mysterious Beast in your inventory. There are a few extra modifiers fully dependent on luck, they are: Rarities: Your mysterious boar can currently be one of three grades: Grand > 9.0 m/s Arcane > 11.5 m/s Celestial > 11.7 m/s Personalities: Your mount can have one of four personalities: Ferocious Hasty Resolute Spunky These personalities determine your mount’s last three abilities. The first 2 abilities of each mount are unaffected by personality and are unique to each species. Species: As stated above, species determine the mount’s first 2 abilities. Once you have your Mysterious Beast, there are a couple of things you can do with it. Let’s use a real example for the sake of simplicity. We just received an Arcane Mysterious Boar from taming a wild boar. Right now your Arcane Mysterious Boar is not yet a mount, it is a sealed, tamed beast. Right now, the only thing you know about it is its base movement speed and its first 2 abilities. In its current form, you may trade it with other players or place it on the auction house. If you prefer to keep it to yourself as a mount then you can unveil your mount to reveal its personality. Upon unveiling your Arcane Mysterious Beast, it can have any of the 4 personalities available. Ferocious Hasty Resolute Spunky As stated earlier, the first 2 abilities of your mount are predetermined by its species. The last 3 abilities are determined by its personality. Each personality has 3 abilities. From the 3rd ability slot to the 5th, each slot is a 50/50 between one ability from its personality pool and one ability from its species. With these in mind, I’m sure you can imagine how many different combinations there are available. Without listing all available abilities, you can think of each personality as a unique archetype: Ferocious has abilities that are offensive and damage oriented. Hasty abilities are focused on speed and covering a lot of distance. Resolute’s ability pool is all about being tanky and surviving as long as possible. Spunky has abilities that are mostly movement oriented. Your last option with your new mount is to release it back into the wild using a Wildcaller Flute, available for purchase from any stablehand. When a mount is released using the Wildcaller Flute, you are granted Whistles of the Wild. The exact amount varies depending on the rarity of the mount released. On average: Grand mounts yield ~3 Whistle of the Wild Arcane mounts yield ~5 Whistle of the Wild Celestial mounts yield ~10 Whistle of the Wild These whistles are crucial to taming as almost every crafting recipe requires them in some amount. On top of already extremely customizable mounts, we have added new custom mount armor sets as well. Each set has 3 pieces; Shaffron (head slot), Saddle (body slot) and Cannonguards (legs slot). And each piece has 3 tiers; base, Regal and Ornate. Currently, there are 4 sets available: Support Stout Survey Swift These sets have unique 3-set bonuses available. Support: Increases mana Regen of all allies, pets and summons within a radius around the mount. Mana regen value and range increases with each tier. (base, Regal, Ornate) Stout: Decreases received damage of the mount and increases damage dealt by the mount. Values increase with each tier. Survey: Increases movement speed when overencumbered. Speed bonus increases with each tier. Swift: Mount ability cooldowns are reduced. The reduction goes up with each tier. Each armor slot requires different materials to craft, however materials do not change between set types. Basic Shaffron (T1): 100x Whistle of the Wild 10x Fabric 10x Duck Down 5x Mysterious Garden Powder Regal Shaffron (T2): 1x Basic Shaffron (T1) 200x Whistle of the Wild 4x Beautifully Colored Fabric 200x Goose Down 50x Earthmana Leaf Ornate Shaffron (T3): 1x Regal Shaffron (T2) 300x Whistle of the Wild 1x Cloudspun Fabric 300x Glossy Feather 3x Lord’s Coin Basic Saddle (T1): 100x Whistle of the Wild 10x Leather 10x Goat Wool 5x Mysterious Garden Powder Regal Saddle (T2): 1x Basic Saddle (T1) 200x Whistle of the Wild 4x Fine Leather 100x Yata Fur 50x Earthmana Leaf Ornate Saddle (T3): 1x Regal Saddle (T2) 300x Whistle of the Wild 1x Wind Spirit Leather 200x Bear Fur 3x Lord’s Coin Basic Cannonguards (T1): 100x Whistle of the Wild 10x Iron Ingot 10x Gold Ingot 5x Mysterious Garden Powder Regal Cannonguards (T2): 1x Basic Cannonguards (T1) 200x Whistle of the Wild 4x Sturdy Ingot 10x Archeum Ingot 50x Earthmana Leaf Ornate Cannonguards (T3): 1x Regal Cannonguards (T2) 300x Whistle of the Wild 1x Sunridge Ingot 20x Anya Ingot 3x Lord’s Coin Alongside armors, there are also new consumables able to be crafted using taming proficiency, These include: Goldscale Dew Stew: -Restores 5.000 mana to your mount over 15 seconds. 1x Hearty Soup 1x Whistle of the Wild 3x Lotus 2x Bay Leaf Greenlord’s Apple: Heals 10.000 health to your mount over 15 seconds. 1x Deluxe Sandwich 1x Whistle of the Wild 10x Apple 1x Scented Leaf Ba-Mana Smoothie Instantly restores all of your mount’s mana. 1x Kraken’s Might 1x Whistle of the Wild 3x Milk 3x Banana Cherry Bomb Instantly fully heals your mount. 1x Nui’s Nova 1x Whistle of the Wild 3x Cherry 3x Impatiens Orange-U-Glad Your mount gains +5.0 movement speed for 7 seconds. 80s cooldown. 1x Flaming Pinion 1x Whistle of the Wild 3x Scented Leaf 5x Pepper 5x Orange 5x Vanilla With the release of 1.3.6: Discovery, there are currently 19 tameable beasts scattered around Erenor. These beasts are as follows: Ant Bat Bladewing Boar Crab Crayfish Earth Elemental Grub Honeybee Jabberwock Mandragora Mantis Owl Razorbeak Scorpion Skyfin Spider Starfish Turtle Taming is the first custom profession and the Archeage Classic team is very excited to hear your feedback on everything. Primal Anthalon (Preview) Primal Anthalon is the latest Primal world boss added to Archeage Classic.
